title: Critical: server start/stop crash and undefined-behaviour bugs
description: Repo review 2026-11-25 group: Critical: server start/stop crash and undefined-behaviour bugs. Items: C1, C2, C3. Source: repo review 2026-11-25 (line numbers as of c2f88df).
close_reason: C1-C3 fixed and verified live (898f472).

title: C1: use-after-free on bind failure in startServer()
description: src/DzScriptServerPane.cpp:801-809. On !is_running() the code deletes m_pServer before m_pServerThread->wait(); the listen thread is still inside m_pServer->listen(). 'Port in use' is a normal error and can crash Studio. Fix: m_pServer->stop(); wait; delete thread; delete server (same order as stopServer()). Extract one teardownServer() helper used by both paths. Source: repo review 2026-11-25 (line numbers as of c2f88df).
close_reason: 898f472. Live DS4 4.24 2026-11-25 on branch quality/yau7-2.17.0: smoke_live iray+viewport 29/29 pass; start on a port held exclusively by another socket failed cleanly (running=false, no crash), then started after release.

title: C2: SSE brokers created after listen thread starts (null deref window)
description: src/DzScriptServerPane.cpp:796 starts the listen thread; m_pEventBroker / m_pRenderProgress are created at :816-820. /scene/events (:1586 registerSubscriber, no null check) or /render/:id/progress hit in that window dereference null on a worker thread. SDK clients that reconnect on restart hit it. Fix: create both brokers before m_pServerThread->start(); set m_bRunning only after everything is constructed. Source: repo review 2026-11-25 (line numbers as of c2f88df).
close_reason: 898f472. Brokers created before the listen thread starts. Live DS4 4.24 2026-11-25 on branch quality/yau7-2.17.0: smoke_live iray+viewport 29/29 pass; stop/start cycles clean. The null-deref window itself isn't directly reproducible.

title: C3: stopServer() can deadlock main thread, then calls QThread::terminate()
description: src/DzScriptServerPane.cpp:870-873. Main thread does wait(5000); HTTP workers blocked in BlockingQueuedConnection calls to the main thread (RequestHandlers.cpp:213,243,315..., plugin routes :1848) can't finish, so wait times out and terminate() kills a thread that may hold locks (UB). Fix: pump events (processEvents(ExcludeUserInputEvents)) until isFinished() or deadline; on timeout log and leak instead of terminate(). Source: repo review 2026-11-25 (line numbers as of c2f88df).
close_reason: 898f472. teardownServer() pumps events while joining, leaks instead of terminate(). Live DS4 4.24 2026-11-25 on branch quality/yau7-2.17.0: smoke_live iray+viewport 29/29 pass; stop -> restart from inside a running async job completed in ~2 s with Studio alive.

title: DS4 crashes on startup: heap corruption in /capabilities snapshot
description: DAZ Studio 4.24 crashed at 'Creating Main Window' (0xc0000374) on every start after a376e47 (5d6f.11). cdb stack: DzScriptServerPane ctor -> startServer -> refreshCapabilitiesSnapshot. Two cross-CRT frees: (1) JsonBuilder::variantToJson called toList() on a QStringList variant; QtCore allocated the QVariant* nodes (msvcr100) and our inline ~QList freed them (ucrtbase). (2) buildCapabilities stored QVariantLists built in our DLL inside a QVariantMap; QtCore's ~QVariant released the last ref and freed our nodes with msvcr100. Fix: StringList branch iterates toStringList(); capabilities JSON is written directly with JsonBuilder (new addKey()) so no DLL-built QVariantList is ever wrapped in a QVariant. Verified: DS4 starts under cdb debug heap, /capabilities OK.
notes: Fix commit: 0b9d708.
close_reason: Fixed in e48b28d; DS4 starts, verified under cdb debug heap

title: render()/render_and_wait() return type change silently breaks truthiness callers
description: dazpy/_render.py:320 - render()/render_and_wait() changed from returning bool (master) to returning a plain RenderOutcome dataclass with no __bool__. Any caller written as 'if rs.render():' (matching the old bool contract, and this is a public SDK method other projects like vangard-daz-mcp depend on) now always evaluates truthy, even when RenderOutcome(success=False, ...) is returned, silently treating failed renders as successful.
acceptance_criteria: Either add __bool__ to RenderOutcome that reflects success, or add a deprecation-safe path so existing truthiness checks behave correctly; document the breaking change in CHANGELOG.md.
close_reason: Added RenderOutcome.__bool__ reflecting success, documented the breaking change in CHANGELOG.md, and added regression tests for truthiness checks.

title: capture() throws ReferenceError on prevBg when backdrop_color is set
description: dazpy/_viewport.py:221 - DazViewport.capture()'s finish_script references the JS variable prevBg, but prevBg is only declared inside the separate prepare_script execute() call (a different HTTP round trip / JS scope). set_bg/restore_bg_js were written for the old single-script version and never had prevBg threaded through the prev_state dict the way selectionName/axesOn etc. were.
acceptance_criteria: capture(path, backdrop_color=(r,g,b)) succeeds (hide_overlays True and False) and restores the original viewport background without throwing.
close_reason: Fixed prevBg round-tripping through prev_state/prep_result JSON instead of a JS var across the two execute() calls; added regression tests for both hide_overlays branches.

title: Stale DzProgress busy sample gives 503 right after a render
description: m_progressBusy (yau7.2 W3) is sampled every 200ms on the main thread. A sample taken inside a render's DzProgress outlives the job by up to one tick, so the next request after a render result gets 503 STUDIO_BUSY 'progress dialog for a foreground operation'. Seen live DS4 2026-11-25: busy at result time (577ms), cleared at 781ms; smoke_live.py iray.engine_readback / iray_samples_readback / viewport.submit failed this way. Fix: pollProgressBusy() right after runDazScript in runCapturedScript, before the result is published.
close_reason: Fixed: pollProgressBusy() after each script run. Verified live 2026-11-25 on DS4 4.24 and DS6 6.26 (smoke_live 29/0 both; hang repro 5/5 Iray renders under 20ms /execute polling).

title: DS4 hangs: Iray /render while /execute is polled every 20ms
description: Live DS4 4.24, plugin ef958c3 (2026-11-25). Repro: scratchpad busy_probe2.py — POST /render engine=iray 64x64 iray_samples=4 on an empty scene while another thread POSTs /execute {script:'1'} every 20ms. The render job stayed 'running' (idle_ms>600000, progress 0); /execute then timed out with no response; Studio window Not Responding with ~idle CPU (deadlock-like, not a slow render). Same render with no concurrent polling completes in ~200-400ms. Suspect: an /execute main-thread call admitted before render.started (busy check passes) runs nested inside doRender's event loop. Not yet root-caused; unknown whether it predates yau7.3. Related: smoke_live.py iray.engine_readback / iray_samples_readback intermittently get 503 STUDIO_BUSY right after a completed Iray render (detail not captured).
close_reason: Fixed: MainThreadCall::ScriptScope defers nested main-thread calls. Verified live 2026-11-25 on DS4 4.24 and DS6 6.26 (smoke_live 29/0 both; hang repro 5/5 Iray renders under 20ms /execute polling).

comments.author: G.Hirpara
comments.text: ROOT CAUSE (procdump + cdb, DS4 4.24, 2026-11-25): main-thread self-deadlock. Main thread stack: processNextAsyncRequest -> runCapturedScript -> runDazScript -> DzScript::execute (render job script) -> QScriptEngine::evaluate -> DzRenderMgr::doCustomRender -> dzirayrenderer -> DzProgress::DzProgress -> QCoreApplication::processEvents -> sendPostedEvents -> handleMainThreadCall -> MainThreadCall::runOnMainThread -> ExecuteScriptHandler lambda -> handleExecuteRequest -> runCapturedScript -> runDazScript -> DzScript::execute -> DzScript::doExecute -> QMutex::lockInternal -> WaitForSingleObject (forever). DzScript::doExecute takes a non-recursive mutex the outer render script already holds on the same thread. The /execute was admitted because the HTTP-thread busy check (broker Rendering flag / 200ms DzProgress sample) passes before the render starts; the queued MainThreadCall then runs inside Iray's DzProgress event pump. Pre-existing; not caused by yau7.3. Fix direction: main-thread re-entrancy guard (depth counter around runDazScript's DzScript::execute/evaluate) checked in MainThreadCall::runOnMainThread, answering 503 STUDIO_BUSY instead of running nested. Dump: scratchpad dumps/ds4_hang.dmp (session-temp).

title: Companion-plugin catch-all routes skip auth, IP whitelist and rate limiter
description: Found while fixing 5d6f.2. applyPluginRoutes() registers /(.*) catch-alls for GET/POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH that dispatch straight to plugin slots (src/DzScriptServerPane.cpp, makeHandler). They run no middleware chain: no token check, no IP whitelist, no rate limit. Any registered companion route (e.g. /export/usd) is reachable without a token. Body size is now capped by set_payload_max_length (5d6f.1). Fix: run m_pWriteChain/m_pReadChain (by method) in makeHandler before dispatch, and check whether existing companion plugins assume unauthenticated access.
acceptance_criteria: Plugin routes require a valid token and honour the IP whitelist; unmatched paths still 404; tests/test_route_security.py covers the catch-alls; companion plugins verified.

(ASSESSMENT #8)

title: Async cancellation reports 'cancelled' before the work actually stops
description: cancelJson sets REQUEST_CANCELLED immediately for RUNNING jobs (src/AsyncRequestManager.cpp:475), even though arbitrary DazScript can't be interrupted and killRender() may find nothing to kill. failStaleRunning does the same with FAILED. If the work finishes later, markCompleted() does nothing and the real outcome is lost. (ASSESSMENT #2)
acceptance_criteria: Distinct states: cancel_requested, cancelled, completed_after_cancel_request (and the stale equivalent); the final real outcome is kept in job history; docs say running scripts can only be cancelled cooperatively; OpenAPI/dazpy/daz-ts status enums updated.
close_reason: cancel_requested/stale/completed_after_* statuses; real outcome kept. Live DS 6.26: script cancel -> cancel_requested -> completed_after_cancel_request; render cancel -> cancel_requested -> cancelled (aborted). OpenAPI/README/dazpy updated; daz-ts follow-up filed.

title: Enforce request body size limit on every POST route
description: BodySizeMiddleware is only attached to m_pExecuteSyncChain (src/DzScriptServerPane.cpp:918). /execute/async, /scripts/:id/async, /scripts/:id/execute, /scripts/register, /render, /render/batch, /render/animation and /scene/save-copy have no body limit. httplib also buffers the whole body before middleware runs, and set_payload_max_length is never called, so the middleware can't stop large bodies being read into memory. (ASSESSMENT #1)
acceptance_criteria: Server calls set_payload_max_length from the configured MB limit; every POST chain includes BodySizeMiddleware (or an equivalent); optional per-endpoint limits for scripts/batches/report metadata; a regression test per endpoint family returns 413.
notes: Done on fix/assessment-p1: set_payload_max_length from config + JSON 413 via set_error_handler; BodySizeMiddleware in the write chain used by every POST/DELETE. Per-endpoint limits (the optional part) not done. Live 413 test per route family in tests/test_api.py (TestStress), not yet run against the new build.

title: IP whitelist and rate limiter are skipped on routes that only use the auth chain
description: Missed by ASSESSMENT.md. /scripts/register, /scripts (GET), /scripts/:id (DELETE), /requests/*, /render/:id/cancel, /render/:id/progress, /scene/save-copy and /scene/events run only m_pAuthChain, so they skip IPWhitelistMiddleware and RateLimitMiddleware. /scene/save-copy writes files to disk. notes: Done on fix/assessment-p1: m_pAuthChain removed; m_pWriteChain (IP+rate+body+auth) for POST/DELETE, m_pReadChain (IP+auth) for polling GETs/SSE. A live whitelist-403 test needs the GUI whitelist enabled, so tests/test_route_security.py checks the route table statically instead (fails 39 subtests on the old code).

title: numpy/OpenBLAS dgemm crash in pinocchio-ik conda env blocks matrix-matrix-multiply tests
description:
## Context
While implementing the Kabsch/Procrustes rotation fix for daz-script-server-ap3l
(finger-posing coordinate misalignment), discovered that numpy matrix-matrix
multiply (2-D `@`/np.dot/np.matmul) reliably crashes with an illegal-instruction
fault (Windows STATUS code 0xc06d007f) in the `pinocchio-ik` conda env
(x:/apps/miniforge3/envs/pinocchio-ik, numpy 2.5.3, OpenBLAS-backed).

Reproduced in isolation: `np.eye(3) @ np.eye(3)` alone crashes. Also crashes:
np.linalg.svd, np.linalg.det, np.linalg.inv, np.linalg.eigh (all use BLAS3/
LAPACK routines like dgemm/dgesdd/dgetrf/dsyevd). Does NOT crash: np.linalg.eig
(dgeev), np.dot on 1-D vectors, matrix-vector products (A @ v), np.cross,
np.outer, np.linalg.norm -- all BLAS1/2, unaffected.

Tried OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS=1, OMP_NUM_THREADS=1, OPENBLAS_CORETYPE=Haswell/
NEHALEM -- none fixed it. Consistent with a known class of OpenBLAS bugs
where runtime CPU-feature dispatch selects an AVX-512 kernel the actual CPU
(or a specific core, on hybrid P/E-core CPUs) doesn't actually support.

## Impact
Two existing tests in ai_vision/pose_transfer_photo/test_finger_ik.py crash
the whole pytest process instead of failing cleanly:
- test_solve_digit_chain_recovers_known_tip_hinge_angle
- test_naive_digit_solve_is_wrong_under_rotated_wrist_but_frame_correction_fixes_it
Both go through pinocchio_ik.py's configuration_from_angles -> bone_local_rotation
-> _compose_euler, which does `R = R @ _axis_rotation(...)` (matrix-matrix).

This also means ANY pipeline code path using 2-D matmul/SVD/det/inv/eigh is a
live crash risk in this conda env, not just these two tests -- worth auditing
pinocchio_ik.py more broadly if this recurs.

## Workaround applied (ap3l only)
finger_ik.py's new kabsch_rotation() was written to avoid all matrix-matrix
multiply/SVD/det/inv, using only cross/dot/outer products instead (a two-vector
exact frame-alignment rotation rather than SVD-based Kabsch). Not applied
elsewhere in pinocchio_ik.py -- those two tests still crash pytest.

## Suggested fix
Reinstall/downgrade numpy and its OpenBLAS backend in the pinocchio-ik conda
env (or switch to an MKL-backed numpy build), then confirm test_finger_ik.py's
full suite (including the two currently-crashing tests) passes clean.
notes:
FIX APPLIED (2026-09-12): set MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 for the pinocchio-ik conda
env.
- Live env: `conda env config vars set MKL_NUM_THREADS=1 -n pinocchio-ik`
- Persisted for reproducibility: added `variables: MKL_NUM_THREADS: "1"` to
  ai_vision/pose_transfer_photo/environment.yml (daz-script-server-examples
  repo), so `conda env create`/`update` reapplies it on any machine.
- Documented in pinocchio_ik.py's module docstring next to the existing
  PATH/DLL segfault note, including the caveat that setting this from
  os.environ inside Python (even before `import numpy`) does NOT work --
  verified empirically that only a shell/process-level env var set before
  python.exe starts takes effect. MKL apparently caches its thread-count
  config from a environment snapshot taken at DLL load, not read lazily
  per-call the way OS-level env inheritance would suggest.

Verified: test_finger_ik.py (28 tests, including the two that previously
crashed the whole pytest process) and test_pinocchio_ik.py (15 tests) both
pass clean via `conda run -n pinocchio-ik pytest ...`, 43/43.

Residual caveat (not fixed, documented instead): raw python.exe invocation
that bypasses `conda activate`/`conda run` still needs the env var set
manually in the calling shell -- conda's env config vars only inject on
activate/run, not on direct interpreter invocation. This is the same
category of gotcha the file already documents for the PATH/DLL issue.
close_reason: Root cause found (MKL multithreading on hybrid P/E-core CPU, not OpenBLAS AVX-512 as originally suspected) and fixed via MKL_NUM_THREADS=1, persisted in environment.yml. 43/43 tests pass.

title: [BUG] DazSceneState.restore() clears conforming clothing/hair fit-to on every skeleton
description:
Discovered while live-verifying daz-pose-indexer's DazpyAdapter.checkpoint()/
restore() (dpi-w55.4) against a real scene (Genesis 9 'Jason Cross' with
fitted clothing/hair -- the dpi-w55.16 reference scene in daz-pose-indexer).
restore() left every conforming item (eyelashes, tear, eyes, mouth,
eyebrows, hair, pants, shirt, boots, jacket -- 10/10 fitted items) visibly
disconnected from the body: gaps at the shoulder/thigh in both the
interactive viewport and a fresh preview render (ruling out a stale-viewport
display issue -- this is a real scene-data change). Cross-referenced as
dpi-kz7 in the daz-pose-indexer beads project.

Read-only diagnosis (querying node.getFollowTarget() via raw DazScript,
before/after each dazpy call in isolation) isolated the exact cause:

- health/discover_scene/find_skeleton_by_label: no effect (read-only, as
  expected).
- DazSceneState.capture(scene) alone: fit-to relationships unaffected --
  all 10 fitted items still read followTarget="Genesis9".
- A plain DazBone.set_local_rotation() on Genesis9's own l_shoulder bone
  alone: fit-to relationships unaffected.
- DazSceneState.apply(scene) (-> DazPose.apply_full() per skeleton): every
  one of the 10 fitted items' followTarget flips to None. Reproduced
  twice (once via a full read/write/restore smoke test, once via an
  apply()-only isolated call).

DESIGN

Root cause hypothesis (not yet confirmed against DAZ Studio's SDK source):
DazSceneState.capture(scene) captures every skeleton in the scene,
including conforming clothing/hair figures. DazPose.apply_full()
(dazpy/_pose.py) does a *full* channel reset per skeleton -- for every
property in `_skel.getNumProperties()` not present in the sparse captured
pose (capture() only stores nonzero raw values), it writes 0 via
setRawValue()/setValue(). If DAZ Studio internally exposes the figure's
"conform to" / follow-target relationship as one of those enumerable
numeric properties (plausible -- many DAZ node relationships are persisted
as properties for save/undo), a skeleton whose fit-to property happened to
not be captured as "nonzero" would get it zeroed by apply_full(), clearing
the relationship. This would affect every conforming item captured via
DazSceneState, not just ones with an actual pose change to restore.

This is a different bug from the earlier checkpoint/restore incident fixed
via independent read-back + retry (StudioBusyError partial-execution --
see daz-pose-indexer's dpi-mxq). This one reproduces cleanly with no busy
contention involved -- it's apply_full()'s "zero every unlisted channel"
semantics doing exactly what they're documented to do, just doing it to a
channel (conform/fit-to) that DazSceneState's per-skeleton bones/morphs/props
capture doesn't know exists and so can never preserve.

Recovery both times was DAZ Studio's own Scene > Revert (fastest, zero
further scripting risk) or reloading the scene file -- NOT further scripted
intervention.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

- Confirm (via DAZ Studio SDK headers/docs, or further isolated live
  testing) whether "conform to" is really exposed via
  DzNode::getNumProperties(), and if so, its property name/id.
- DazSceneState.capture()/apply() preserves each captured skeleton's
  conforming follow-target across a checkpoint/restore cycle, verified
  against the Jason Cross reference scene with a fresh before/after
  getFollowTarget() diff over all fitted items.
- Regression test added (mirroring tests/test_dazpy.py::TestDazSceneStateApply)
  covering a scene with at least one conforming item, asserting
  getFollowTarget() is unchanged after capture()/apply().
design:
CONFIRMED ROOT CAUSE (2026-08-21, live isolation testing against
DazScriptServer 2.9.1, Genesis 9 "Jason Cross" scene, BR_Boots item only --
minimal blast radius, self-healed after each step):

1. A single conforming item's own DazPose.capture(boots_skeleton) ->
   apply_full(boots_skeleton) round trip (no other skeleton touched, not
   through DazSceneState at all) is sufficient to reproduce: followTarget
   flips from "Genesis9" to None, with zero bone/morph pose change (boots
   was at rest -- capture() returned bones={}, morphs={}).
2. The captured props dict included `'FID_BR_Boots_18686': 1` -- almost
   certainly the internal property DAZ Studio uses to persist this item's
   fit/conform registration (name pattern: "FID_<this node's own name>").
   apply_full() writes this back via setRawValue(1) -- the exact same
   value that was captured. Despite the persisted raw value round-tripping
   identically, the live in-memory getFollowTarget() pointer still breaks.
3. Conclusion: rewriting a "FID_*" property (regardless of value) does not
   go through whatever internal resolution DAZ Studio uses to establish
   the live follow-target pointer (that likely only happens via the actual
   setFollowTarget() slot / scene-load-time resolution, not a generic
   property write). DazPose.apply_full()'s blanket "write back every
   property on this skeleton, zero if uncaptured" semantics doesn't know
   FID_* is special and corrupts it as a side effect even when round-
   tripping the identical value.

Isolated via elimination (all against the same BR_Boots item, each
verified + self-healed before the next):
- capture() alone: no effect.
- DazBone.set_local_rotation() (computed/setValue path) on one of boots'
  own bones: no effect.
- A raw setRawValue() write to one bone's rotation control: no effect.
- DazPose.apply_full(boots) (writes back captured bones+morphs+props,
  including FID_BR_Boots_18686): breaks followTarget every time.

Recovery used each time: dazpy's own `node.fit_to(figure)` (calls
setFollowTarget() through the sanctioned API) -- confirmed via a fresh
preview render that conforming is visually correct again afterward. This
is a much safer/more surgical recovery than the DAZ Studio Revert used in
the original whole-scene incidents, since it's scoped to exactly the item
that broke and uses dazpy's own supported API.

PROPOSED FIX (not yet implemented)

DazSceneState already iterates every skeleton in the scene structurally,
so it's the natural place to fix this rather than DazPose generically:

1. DazSceneState.capture(scene): additionally record each skeleton's
   `skel.getFollowTarget()` (by name, or None) in a new field, e.g.
   `follow_targets: dict[str, str | None]`.
2. DazSceneState.apply(scene): after a skeleton's pose is restored and
   verified (existing dpi-mxq logic), explicitly call
   `skel.setFollowTarget(<resolved target skeleton>)` to restore the
   conform relationship -- using the real API, not relying on FID_*
   round-tripping correctly. Skip for skeletons with no captured target.
3. Regression test (mirrors tests/test_dazpy.py::TestDazSceneStateApply):
   a scene with at least one conforming item, asserting getFollowTarget()
   is unchanged after a capture()/apply() cycle even when the base
   figure's pose actually changes.

Open question the header alone couldn't answer: whether "FID_*" should
also just be excluded from DazPose's own generic capture/apply (a second,
independent layer of defense for callers using DazPose directly on a
conforming item without going through DazSceneState) -- worth doing too,
since apply_full()'s docstring promises a "clean, authoritative reset"
that currently corrupts conforming state as an undocumented side effect.
notes:
FIX IMPLEMENTED AND VALIDATED (2026-08-21).

Changes (dazpy/_scene_state.py):
- DazSceneState gained a `follow_targets: dict[str, str | None]` field,
  captured alongside skeleton_poses in capture() via each skeleton's
  follow_target() (not inferred from generic properties).
- apply() now does an explicit follow-target restoration pass after the
  existing pose-restore/verify loop: for each successfully-restored
  skeleton whose live follow_target() no longer matches what was
  captured, calls unfit() (captured target was None) or fit_to() (captured
  a specific target) via the real API -- not a raw property write.
- Added a local _retry_on_busy() helper (mirrors DazClient's backoff) and
  wired it around the follow-target read/write calls and the final
  camera/light restore_script call, since driving 11 skeletons through
  pose-restore + verify + follow-target-fix in one apply() call is enough
  HTTP volume to transiently hit StudioBusyError on individual calls that
  didn't previously retry.
- to_dict()/from_dict() updated for the new field (backward compatible --
  defaults to {} for old serialized checkpoints).

Tests: 4 new unit tests in TestDazSceneStateApply (tests/test_dazpy.py) --
restores a desynced follow-target, skips when already correct, unfits when
captured target was None, and retries on a transient StudioBusyError
during the follow-target pass. All 683 unit tests in test_dazpy.py pass.

LIVE VALIDATION (Genesis 9 "Jason Cross" scene, BR_Boots + full 11-skeleton
scene):
1. Single-skeleton repro (DazPose.capture(boots)+apply_full(boots) with
   no fix): followTarget flips to None every time, as originally found.
2. Same single-skeleton case through DazSceneState with the fix: 
   followTarget stays "Genesis9" -- confirmed via getFollowTarget() query
   and a fresh preview render (boots fit correctly).
3. Full-scene checkpoint()/write_channels()/restore() (the original
   dpi-w55.4 smoke-test scenario, all 11 skeletons): fit-to relationships
   for all 10 conforming items held across two consecutive live attempts
   -- including one where the overall restore() call raised due to an
   unrelated find_skeleton() busy error late in the run (a separate,
   pre-existing gap, not part of this bug -- find_skeleton() itself has
   no retry_on_busy option). The follow-target fix itself did not
   regress in either case.
4. Root cause confirmed precisely: captured props included
   `FID_BR_Boots_18686: 1` (the item's own fit-registration property).
   apply_full() writes that back via setRawValue() at the *same* captured
   value, yet the live getFollowTarget() pointer still breaks -- rewriting
   FID_* does not go through whatever internal resolution actually
   establishes the pointer.

Known related gap NOT covered by this fix (separate from dpi-kz7's actual
follow-target bug, tracked here only as a note): scene.find_skeleton()
and DazPose.capture()'s verify read-back call have no retry_on_busy
option, so a very busy server can still cause apply() to report a
skeleton as failed-to-restore. Worth a follow-up bead if it recurs.
close_reason: Fixed in dazpy/_scene_state.py: DazSceneState.capture()/apply() now capture and restore each skeleton's conform/fit-to relationship explicitly via getFollowTarget()/fit_to()/unfit(), independent of DazPose's generic property capture (which was silently desyncing the live follow-target pointer via its FID_* property rewrite). 4 new regression tests added; all 683 unit tests pass; fix live-validated twice against the Jason Cross reference scene (single-skeleton and full 11-skeleton checkpoint/restore).

title: fix: render success reporting trusted doRender()'s undocumented return value
description: dazpy.DazRenderSettings.render() derived success from doRender()'s return code (err === 0 || err === true), but the DAZ SDK docs have no Returns: section for doRender() at all. Live testing showed it reports success even for a render the user cancelled mid-progress via the DAZ Studio UI. The async render endpoints in src/DzScriptServerPane.cpp (buildRenderScript/buildAnimationRenderScript, backing /render/submit and /render/animation) were worse -- they didn't check the return value at all and hardcoded success:true unconditionally, even on cancel/failure.
design: Both now derive success from DzRenderMgr.renderFinished(bool succeeded), the SDK's named completion signal, already trusted in SceneEventBroker.cpp as the guaranteed exit path across error/cancel cases. Confirmed live that DazScript can connect to it: mgr["renderFinished(bool)"].connect(fn). Animation loop tracks per-frame success and ANDs them for overall success.
acceptance_criteria: dazpy render() and the C++ async render script builders report success based on renderFinished(bool), not doRender()'s return code. Verified live for the completed-render case; full verification of the cancelled-render case pending a DAZ Studio restart to pick up the rebuilt plugin DLL.
close_reason: Verified live: restarted DAZ Studio to load the rebuilt plugin, then reproduced the exact original bug scenario (real render, user clicks Cancel in the DAZ Studio progress dialog ~6s in) via dazpy render(). RenderOutcome now correctly reports success=False (previously reported success=True in this exact scenario). Confirmed by hasRender()=false and the saved output being an unconverged blank frame, both consistent with genuine cancellation.

title: fix(dazpy): render() must pin Active Canvas to Beauty (GH #32 clown render)
description: GitHub issue #32: enabling Iray Canvases programmatically corrupts the primary saved beauty render into a MaterialID-style 'clown render'. Root cause: DzIrayPropertyHolder.findCanvasDefinition(name, true) implicitly reassigns the 'Active Canvas' enum property to whichever canvas was most recently created/looked-up (confirmed live against DAZ Studio). Once any non-Beauty canvas exists, doRender() saves that canvas's pass as the primary output file instead of the true beauty image. Fixed by forcing Active Canvas back to 'Beauty' (creating it if missing) inside render() right before doRender() whenever renderToCanvases is on.
acceptance_criteria: render() always saves the true beauty pass as the primary output_path regardless of which canvas was last created/active when canvases_enabled is true. Verified live against DAZ Studio: switching Active Canvas to a MaterialID canvas before calling render() no longer corrupts the saved beauty image.
close_reason: Fixed in dazpy/_render.py render(): force Active Canvas back to Beauty before doRender() whenever renderToCanvases is enabled. Verified live against DAZ Studio and covered by a regression test.

title: Async render request stuck at 'running' forever on render failure (GH #34)
description: AsyncRequestManager has no watchdog/timeout that fails a stale 'running' render request. If the render never signals completion (blocked behind DAZ Studio's modal error dialog), GET /requests/:id stays 'running' indefinitely with no way for a client to detect failure short of a very long wait. Add either: (a) a render-error signal handler that resolves the request as 'failed' with the error message, or (b) a timeout that marks it failed after a bound. Depends on daz-script-server-3l5o to correctly detect the failure condition. (GH issue #34, suggestion #2)
acceptance_criteria: A render that errors resolves the async request to 'failed' (with a useful error message) within a bounded time, instead of staying 'running' indefinitely.
close_reason: Closed

title: Render busy state never clears on failed/error render (GH #34)
description: SceneEventBroker only wires enterBusy()/exitBusy() to aboutToRender/renderFinished (SceneEventBroker.cpp:114-116). When a render errors, DAZ Studio pops a blocking modal and renderFinished never fires, so exitBusy() is never called and the plugin's busy counter stays stuck. Every subsequent /execute then returns 503 forever, recoverable only by restarting DAZ Studio. This is the root cause and the highest-leverage fix (GH issue #34, suggestion #1).
acceptance_criteria: A render that ends in error/abort no longer leaves the plugin permanently busy; /execute succeeds again without restarting DAZ Studio. exitBusy() fires on every render termination path, not just the success path.
notes:
Live-verified on running DAZ Studio 4 instance (2026-08-14): submitted an async render to a nonexistent drive (A:/...) via /render. Render itself succeeded (Iray converged to 97%), but the file-save step failed and DAZ Studio popped a blocking 'Error Saving' modal (Try Again / Choose New File / Cancel). While the modal was up, /execute correctly fail-fast'd with 503 STUDIO_BUSY (not a hang) and /health stayed responsive. After clicking Cancel on the modal, /execute immediately returned 200 and the async request transitioned running -> completed -- no DAZ Studio restart needed. Confirms DzRenderMgr::renderFinished(bool) fires as the guaranteed exit signal even on this non-happy-path outcome.

Also live-verified on DAZ Studio 6 (2026-08-14) with the identical procedure (nonexistent-drive output_path -> render succeeds, save fails, 'Error Saving' modal blocks main thread -> /execute correctly 503s STUDIO_BUSY while blocked, not hung -> after clicking Cancel, /execute immediately 200s and request transitions running -> completed). Confirms the fix holds across both SDK4 and SDK6 builds.

Note: this save-failure trick reproduces the same class of bug as the GH issue (a non-happy-path render outcome that pops a blocking modal), not the exact Iray-engine-failure repro (Scene.setBackdrop(null) -> Iray DB transaction abort). Attempted that exact repro separately on both DS4 and DS6 -- it hard-crashed both, with two DIFFERENT ACCESS_VIOLATION signatures (DzBackdrop::isVisible() on DS4, DzStyledTimeAsFramesPropertyWgt::~DzStyledTimeAsFramesPropertyWgt() on DS6), confirming Scene.setBackdrop(null) is a distinct, pre-existing DAZ Studio bug unrelated to this plugin and unsafe to use for live testing (see memory feedback_dazscript_blocking_dialogs). The save-failure repro is the safe, repeatable way to exercise this exact code path.
close_reason: Closed

title: Live-verify dazpy.lighting _look_at_euler yaw sign against real DAZ Studio
description:
Final whole-branch review of daz-script-server-p1af's ThreePointLightSetup work found that _look_at_euler's yaw formula in dazpy/lighting.py is likely sign-inverted for off-axis lights (nonzero X component in the aim direction -- this includes the default rig's key and fill lights, only the rim light at azimuth=180 is unaffected). Independently re-derived via dazpy/math3.py's own _euler_to_quat XYZ rotation convention (documented to match DAZ's bone-rotation channels): the correct formula is yaw = atan2(-direction.x, -direction.z), not the current atan2(direction.x, -direction.z). This derivation is solid but has NOT been empirically confirmed against a live DAZ Studio session, because no server was reachable during review (generic node rotation-control composition order was assumed to match the bone convention, but not independently confirmed for DzSpotLight/DzDistantLight/DzPointLight). Per user decision, the sign flip was deliberately withheld pending live verification rather than applied blind.

Action: with DAZ Studio running, create a rig via apply_three_point_light_setup at a known azimuth (e.g. 90) against a known target, then call DazLight.direction() on the resulting light and confirm it points at the target. If direction() confirms the current code's -90 deg is wrong and +90 is correct, apply the one-line fix (dazpy/lighting.py, the yaw calculation in _look_at_euler) and update test_look_at_euler_yaws_toward_90_azimuth_offset's expected value from -90.0 to +90.0 in tests/test_dazpy.py. If the live check instead confirms the current sign is correct, remove the caveat docstring note and close this without a code change.
close_reason: Confirmed live against running DAZ Studio: distant light rotated to y=+90 reports DazLight.direction()=(-1,0,~0), matching the intended convention; prior y=-90 was inverted. Fix applied and committed to feature/dazpy-lighting (commit f26e571). Full suite 557/557 passing.

title: Reintroduce face-region pass for LoRA-intensity control (no identity conditioning)
description:
Live-tuning against jason_a/abby_b (daz-script-server-r5br) found a new artifact after 3os's rebuild: the Graphic_Novel style LoRA at full strength (0.8) draws harsh 'pencil mark' ink lines on facial features (brow ridge, under-eye, under-nose) that read as artifactual rather than stylistic, confirmed by isolating lora_strength=0.0 (marks vanish entirely) vs 0.8 (marks present) with all ControlNet/composite settings held constant -- ruled out Canny threshold, composite opacity, and controlnet_lineart_weight as causes first (all had negligible effect). Lowering lora_strength globally (tested 0.3-0.6) fixes the face but also strips most of the body's ink-hatching texture, since the current architecture (post-3os) is a single full-image pass -- there's no way to apply a different LoRA intensity to the face vs body.

Root cause: faces read 'harsher' than bodies at any single style intensity (high-frequency geometric detail vs. smooth clothing), the same tension that originally motivated the FaceDetailer/IPAdapterFaceID branch this epic's rebuild (3os) removed. That removal correctly fixed toe's specific artifacts (traced to IPAdapterFaceID/SEGSDetailer's identity-conditioning behavior at denoise=0.35/faceid_weight=1.0), but didn't address the underlying face/body intensity mismatch -- it just removed the only mechanism that let the two differ.

Fix: reintroduce a face-region crop+resample pass, reusing the parts of the old mechanism that were never implicated in toe (face bbox/SAM detection via UltralyticsDetectorProvider+SAMDetectorCombined, and the per-region ControlNet chain via ImpactControlNetApplyAdvancedSEGS -- both confirmed innocent by toe's zero-baseline test, which disabled the whole face-refinement chain and still reproduced the artifacts). Explicitly exclude IPAdapterFaceID/IPAdapterInsightFaceLoader/IPAdapterUnifiedLoaderFaceID entirely -- no identity conditioning of any kind. New mechanism: a second LoraLoader patched at a lower strength than the main pass, feeding SEGSDetailer for the face crop resample, so face and body get independently tunable LoRA intensity.
design:
workflow_controlnet.json: add back UltralyticsDetectorProvider, BboxDetectorSEGS, SAMLoader, SAMDetectorCombined, MaskToSEGS, 3x ImpactControlNetApplyAdvancedSEGS (normal/depth/lineart), SEGSDetailer, SEGSPaste -- same node shapes as the pre-3os workflow (see git show 04b6274~1:docs/examples/rendering/sprite_matrix/workflow_controlnet.json for reference), but with a NEW second LoraLoader node (patched at face_pass_lora_strength) feeding SEGSDetailer's basic_pipe instead of IPAdapterFaceID's output. No IPAdapter/InsightFace nodes at all.

New config.py fields on ComfyUIStageConfig: face_pass_enabled (bool), face_pass_lora_strength (float), face_pass_denoise (float), face_pass_guide_size (float), face_pass_bbox_dilation (int), face_pass_controlnet_normal_weight/depth_weight/lineart_weight (float) -- reuse the old face_detailer_* naming pattern minus faceid_weight (no identity conditioning to tune). Thread through schema.py, render_shot.py CLI, stylize_stage.py, workflow_builder.py following the same pattern as the removed face_detailer_* fields.

Live-tune face_pass_lora_strength against jason_a and abby_b once wired up -- 0.5 looked promising in ad-hoc testing during r5br but wasn't tested through the actual crop/paste mechanism, only as a global override.
acceptance_criteria: Face renders without harsh pencil-mark lines (brow ridge, under-eye, under-nose) on both jason_a and abby_b. Body retains full ink-hatching texture (main pass LoRA strength unchanged from whatever was chosen for body). No identity-conditioning artifacts reintroduced (toe stays fixed) -- verify since this does bring back SEGSDetailer, which was part of the original toe-implicated chain even though the root cause was specifically IPAdapterFaceID/faceid conditioning, not SEGSDetailer itself.
close_reason: Abandoned in favor of a simpler fix. Root cause was correctly diagnosed (Graphic_Novel LoRA draws harsh ink lines on facial creases at full strength) but the proposed face-region-pass fix backfired when tested: reusing the old per-region ControlNet weights (1.4/1.1/0.9, tuned for a different context with identity-locked low stylization) fought against the new lower-strength face LoRA and produced worse artifacts (heavy dark under-eye blocking), unresponsive to further LoRA reduction. Superseded by daz-script-server-r5br's negative-prompt suppression fix, which resolves the same root cause with zero architecture change. workflow_controlnet.json/workflow_builder.py changes from this issue were reverted.

title: Live-tune lineart_composite_opacity and validate toe/a5o resolved
description: Part of daz-script-server-3os. Once the rebuild is wired up (daz-script-server-7f2, -4a0, -5do, -pxmn), live-test against abby_b and jason_a: confirm daz-script-server-toe's artifacts (pale/ghostlike skin, harsh eye-shadow split) are gone; confirm facial identity is still recognizable without IPAdapterFaceID conditioning (the accepted trade-off of this rebuild); confirm daz-script-server-a5o (hair color drift) is resolved as a side effect; tune lineart_composite_opacity if full-strength (1.0) reads as over-inked/noisy on skin. Close toe and a5o once confirmed, or reopen/adjust design if identity loss is unacceptable.
acceptance_criteria: Live-verified against both abby_b and jason_a. Final lineart_composite_opacity value chosen and recorded in config.py comments. toe and a5o closed with reference to this validation, or a documented follow-up filed if identity conditioning needs to be reintroduced some other way.
notes: CORRECTION after initial close: 120/240 Canny thresholds still left small isolated stray marks (forehead, eyebrow tip, under-lip) on jason_a, visible at high zoom -- caught by user review of the copied final images. Isolated the residual cause (now that the LoRA's own line-drawing was already suppressed): tiny high-contrast points in the Iray render (specular highlights, skin pores) still exceeding even 120/240 in isolated spots. Tested 150/300, 200/400, and bilateral-filter pre-smoothing against a clean (negative-prompt-fixed) baseline -- all three cleared the residual marks equally well, so picked 150/300 as the more conservative change with no bilateral-filter complexity needed. Final default is 150/300, not 120/240. Re-verified through the actual production CLI (render_shot.py) at 3x zoom on both jason_a and abby_b -- clean.
close_reason:
Final fix has two parts, both live-verified against jason_a and abby_b through the actual production pipeline (render_shot.py):
1. Negative-prompt suppression (config.py ComfyUIStageConfig.negative_prompt): added terms against harsh facial crosshatching/under-eye ink/exaggerated brow lines. Root cause: the Graphic_Novel LoRA at full strength (0.8) draws ink strokes along facial creases as a learned stylistic behavior (confirmed via isolating lora_strength=0.0 vs 0.8 with all else held constant) -- promptable away without any architecture change or LoRA/body-hatching tradeoff.
2. Canny threshold retune (canvas_convert.derive_lineart default 80/160 -> 120/240, now also exposed as config/CLI knobs -- see daz-script-server-017n): removes the residual contribution from real Iray shading-edge lines (brow ridge, under-nose) picked up by the deterministic lineart composite pass, independent of the LoRA behavior.
Both were needed together -- prompt suppression alone left a faint under-nose/brow line from the composite step; threshold retune alone (tested earlier) didn't fully clear the LoRA-drawn lines.
lineart_composite_opacity stays at 1.0 (no longer needs lowering now that both upstream sources are addressed).
A face-region-pass approach (daz-script-server-fsq8) was attempted and abandoned -- see that issue's close reason.

title: Update sprite_matrix config.py: remove face_detailer_* fields, add lineart_composite_opacity
description: Part of daz-script-server-3os. title: Rebuild face stylization as line-color-split composite (replace FaceDetailer/IPAdapterFaceID)
description: Root-cause work on daz-script-server-toe traced the pale/ghostlike-skin and harsh-shadow artifacts to the IPAdapterFaceID face-identity pass itself (denoise=0.35, faceid_weight=1.0), confirmed via a live zero-baseline test with the per-region ControlNet chain fully disabled (artifacts persisted). Rather than continue tuning that node's knobs, replace the two-pass architecture (main KSampler + SEGSDetailer/IPAdapterFaceID face refinement) with a single full-image KSampler pass followed by a deterministic post-process composite: multiply-blend the existing Canny lineart (canvas_convert.py derive_lineart(), already used as a ControlNet guide) over the color output. This decouples linework fidelity from diffusion sampling entirely, so neither pass's artifacts can desync face/body style. Design discussed and approved 2026-08-06 (no separate spec doc; captured here in bd).
design: Architecture: DAZ beauty render -> Canny lineart (unchanged derive_lineart) + Normal/Depth -> ComfyUI [LoRA + 3x ControlNetApply + KSampler + VAEDecode] -> stylize_stage.py multiply_blend(color, lineart_png, opacity) -> final output. Remove FaceDetailer/IPAdapterFaceID chain entirely (nodes 60,62,64-75 in workflow_controlnet.json): UltralyticsDetectorProvider, BboxDetectorSEGS, SAMLoader/SAMDetectorCombined, MaskToSEGS, 3x ImpactControlNetApplyAdvancedSEGS, IPAdapterInsightFaceLoader/IPAdapterUnifiedLoaderFaceID/IPAdapterFaceID, SEGSDetailer, SEGSPaste. SaveImage now saves the composited result. New config.py knob: lineart_composite_opacity (float, default 1.0). Removed config knobs: face_detailer_enabled/denoise/guide_size/bbox_dilation/faceid_weight/controlnet_normal_weight/controlnet_depth_weight/controlnet_lineart_weight. Trade-off accepted: no explicit facial-identity conditioning after this change -- likeness depends entirely on main pass's low denoise (0.35) + ControlNet; must be live-verified, not just assumed.
acceptance_criteria: Both toe artifacts (pale/ghostlike skin, harsh eye-shadow split) gone on abby_b and jason_a. Facial identity still recognizable without IPAdapterFaceID conditioning. daz-script-server-a5o (hair color drift) confirmed resolved as a side effect. lineart_composite_opacity tuned to a value that doesn't read as over-inked/noisy on flat skin regions.
close_reason: All subtasks complete (7f2, 4a0, pxmn, 5do). Rebuild live-verified against jason_a and abby_b; a follow-up artifact surfaced during that live-tuning (harsh facial ink lines from the style LoRA) was tracked and resolved separately as daz-script-server-r5br/017n.

title: Face-identity pass produces unnatural facial artifacts (pale/ghostlike skin, harsh eye shadows)
description: Live testing (post per-region-ControlNet merge) found the face-identity pass produces unnatural results: abby_b's face renders flat/pale/porcelain-like with stark black nostrils and a vacant stare ('ghost like'); jason_a's face shows harsh, unnatural dark under-eye/split-face shadowing not present in the source Daz beauty render. CONFIRMED via a live zero-baseline test (face_detailer_controlnet_*_weight all set to 0.0, i.e. the per-region ControlNet chain contributing nothing): both artifacts are present even with the new ControlNet chain fully disabled. This means the per-region ControlNet work (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-05-face-detailer-controlnet.md) is NOT the cause -- the root cause traces back further, to the already-merged FaceID conditioning branch's settings (face_detailer_denoise=0.35, face_detailer_faceid_weight=1.0, docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-05-faceid-conditioning.md).
acceptance_criteria: Root cause identified (likely denoise or faceid_weight interaction, possibly IPAdapter FaceID's own behavior at these settings). New defaults chosen and live-verified against both abby_b and jason_a to no longer show these artifacts, without reintroducing the original photoreal-face-vs-hatched-body mismatch that motivated the FaceID and ControlNet work in the first place.
notes: Session ended before this was investigated further -- pick up with the FaceID/denoise settings specifically, not the ControlNet weights (already ruled out via the zero-baseline test). Consider: try lower denoise (below 0.35) and/or lower faceid_weight (below 1.0) combinations; check whether this is an IPAdapterFaceID node-level behavior (e.g. weight_type/embeds_scaling fixed literals in workflow_controlnet.json) rather than just the tunable knobs.
close_reason: Confirmed resolved via live testing against jason_a and abby_b, following the daz-script-server-3os rebuild (single-pass + lineart composite, replacing FaceDetailer/IPAdapterFaceID) and the r5br negative-prompt/Canny-threshold follow-up fix for a newly-surfaced artifact (harsh facial ink lines from the style LoRA, distinct from toe's original pale-skin/split-shadow symptoms but found during the same live-tuning pass). No pale/ghostlike skin, no harsh eye-shadow, no facial pencil-mark lines, no hair-color seam artifact (no more crop boundary to desync at) on either character.

title: Fix background box artifact in face-identity pass via SAM silhouette masking
description: Live testing showed a rectangular 'box' artifact behind the head/shoulders in stylized output: bbox_dilation=100 (added to fix the hair-color seam) pulled surrounding black background into the face-detailer crop region, which SEGSDetailer then subtly re-stylized (measured: background outside the crop stayed ~[5,4,4] pure black, inside the crop rose to ~[37,40,54] with high noise). Root cause: face_yolov8m.pt is bbox-only (confirmed via Impact-Subpack source -- SEGM_DETECTOR output is a NO_SEGM_DETECTOR() stub for bbox-only models), so BboxDetectorSEGS's noise mask is always a plain dilated rectangle, not a silhouette -- dilating enough to cover the hair inherently also covers surrounding background. Fixed by refining that rectangular hint into an actual head/hair silhouette via SAM (SAMLoader + SAMDetectorCombined with bbox_expansion=80/dilation=60 + MaskToSEGS with bbox_fill=false) before the crop-source swap. Verified live via precise pixel sampling: background pixels immediately outside the hair silhouette are pure black in every direction, while hair color remains correctly identity-preserved throughout (no regression of the earlier seam fix). Required an existing sam_vit_b_01ec64.pth model already present in the live ComfyUI instance -- no new downloads needed this time.
close_reason: Fixed and verified against live DAZ Studio + ComfyUI via precise pixel sampling: no residual box artifact, hair-color fix preserved. 647 tests passing.

title: Fix hair-color seam in face-identity pass via generous bbox dilation
description: Live testing revealed a visible color seam at the hairline in stylized output: the face detector's bbox (UltralyticsDetectorProvider/face_yolov8m.pt) only covers eyes/nose/mouth/forehead, not the crown of the hair, so SEGSPaste only replaced the lower portion of the head with identity-preserved pixels -- the crown kept the main pass's invented (different) hair color, creating a hard two-tone boundary. Fixed by exposing bbox_dilation as a configurable parameter (comfyui.face_detailer.bbox_dilation in spec / --face-detailer-bbox-dilation CLI flag) defaulting to 100px (up from the node's own default of 10px), which pushes the refined/pasted region up through the whole head. Verified live: dilation=100 eliminates the seam.
close_reason: Fixed and verified against live DAZ Studio + ComfyUI; hair color now consistent throughout with default bbox_dilation=100. 646 tests passing.

title: Add face-identity preservation pass to sprite matrix ComfyUI workflow
description: Adds a second-pass face refinement to the stylize workflow: detects the face in the stylized output via UltralyticsDetectorProvider (bbox/face_yolov8m.pt), but critically swaps the crop's pixel source to the ORIGINAL Daz beauty render (not the already-stylized/drifted output) via SetDefaultImageForSEGS before refining at lower denoise via SEGSDetailer, then composites back via SEGSPaste. An earlier all-in-one FaceDetailer node version was tried first but confirmed (live, visually) to only polish the already-drifted face since it detects+crops+refines from the same (stylized) image -- this SEGS-based version fixes that by explicitly re-sourcing the crop pixels. New comfyui.face_detailer spec fields (enabled/denoise/guide_size) and render_shot.py --face-detailer/--no-face-detailer/--face-detailer-denoise/--face-detailer-guide-size flags. Required installing ComfyUI's Impact-Subpack custom node (UltralyticsDetectorProvider) and downloading bbox/face_yolov8m.pt into the live ComfyUI instance -- environment-side setup, documented in sprite_matrix/README.md.
close_reason: Implemented, verified against live DAZ Studio + ComfyUI: face now closely matches original Daz character identity (hair color, expression) instead of drifting. 644 tests passing.

title: Fix Iray Canvas beauty-image corruption and cross-directory test module collisions
description: (1) Live smoke test found DazRenderSettings.render() with canvases_enabled=True writes canvas content (e.g. a Normal map) as the primary saved image instead of the true beauty composite -- confirmed with/without an explicit Beauty canvas, isolated to canvases_enabled itself. Added render_util.render_beauty_and_canvases() workaround: render once with canvases enabled (correct AOV EXRs), then again with canvases disabled to the same path (overwrites corrupted beauty PNG, leaves EXRs untouched). Wired into render_stage.py and render_shot.py. (2) Running sprite_matrix and comfyui_enhance tests in the same pytest process surfaced sys.modules collisions: both docs/examples/rendering/{comfyui_enhance,sprite_matrix}/ define same-named workflow_builder.py and config.py with incompatible contents, so whichever test file imports first silently wins for all others. Added defensive sys.modules eviction before each affected test's local imports. Also fixed a separate pre-existing bug: 3 comfyui_enhance test files pointed sys.path at a stale nonexistent 'examples/comfyui_enhance' directory (real path is docs/examples/rendering/comfyui_enhance) -- these tests were silently broken standalone before this fix.
close_reason: Both fixed and verified: full end-to-end run against live Daz+ComfyUI now produces a correct beauty render and correct stylized output; test collision confirmed resolved across multiple collection orderings (630 passed, 1 skipped).

title: Fix sprite matrix pipeline bugs found during live smoke test
description: Live end-to-end run against real DAZ Studio + ComfyUI surfaced 4 real bugs: (1) DazRenderSettings.render(camera_name=...) resolves by internal node name via Scene.findCamera(), which is not guaranteed unique (duplicating a camera in the Scene panel copies its internal name too) -- added camera_label param using Scene.findCameraByLabel() instead, which DAZ Studio keeps unique. (2) Mixed forward/backslash paths (output_dir passed with '/' on Windows, then os.path.join appending '\') broke DAZ's Iray Canvas output-path derivation, causing canvas EXRs to land in a doubled nested directory -- paths.py now normalizes every returned path via os.path.normpath. (3) opencv-python ships OpenEXR support disabled by default -- canvas_convert.py now sets OPENCV_IO_ENABLE_OPENEXR=1 before importing cv2. (4) ComfyUI's LoraLoader rejects an empty lora_name outright when zero LoRAs are installed (dropdown enum is []) -- workflow_builder.py now drops the LoraLoader node entirely and rewires its consumers to the checkpoint when no LoRA is configured.
close_reason: Fixed all 4 issues; verified against live DAZ Studio + ComfyUI instance and full test suite (597 passed).

Build dsp_runner: a small Python module bundled into every package venv that imports the entry point, calls its run(inputs) function with stdout redirected (reusing daemon/worker_runtime.py's hardening pattern), and prints one final {success,result,output,error} JSON envelope line. title: DazPose.apply_full() doesn't zero absent node properties
description: dazpy/_pose.py:352 - apply_full()'s node-property loop only calls setValue/setRawValue 'if (v !== undefined)', with no else-zero branch, unlike the bones loop (lines 327-331: explicit else setValue(0)) and morphs loop (line 344: _v = v !== undefined ? v : 0) right above it in the same function. The docstring promises 'every bone rotation, morph, and node property... is explicitly set -- channels absent from the pose are driven to zero,' but sparse-captured (zero-valued, omitted) node properties are left unchanged instead of reverting to 0 on apply_full(). This also affects DazSceneState.apply()'s 'clean baseline' restore, which relies on apply_full().
acceptance_criteria: Node-property loop in apply_full() zeroes properties absent from the captured pose, matching the bones/morphs pattern. Add a test: capture with a node property at 0, change it, apply_full(), assert it reverts to 0.
close_reason: Node-property loop in apply_full() now falls back to 0 like the bones/morphs loops, matching the documented contract; added a regression test.

title: DazSceneState.apply() doesn't isolate apply_full() errors per skeleton
description: dazpy/_scene_state.py:185 - apply()'s per-skeleton try/except only wraps scene.find_skeleton(name); the following pose.apply_full(skel) call sits outside that try block. The docstring promises 'Nodes that no longer exist in the scene are skipped and reported in errors rather than raising.' If apply_full() raises for any skeleton (transient HTTP/DazScript execution error, stale skeleton reference), the exception propagates uncaught and aborts restoration of all remaining skeletons, cameras, and lights.
acceptance_criteria: Wrap pose.apply_full(skel) in the same try/except as find_skeleton, appending to errors and continuing to the next skeleton/camera/light on failure. Add a test exercising a mid-loop failure.
close_reason: Wrapped pose.apply_full() in its own try/except alongside find_skeleton's, so a mid-loop failure is recorded in errors and restoration continues; added two regression tests.

title: build_hug_recipe() swaps far-shoulder targets between actors
description: dazpy/_interaction.py:1857 - build_hug_recipe() computes a_far_shoulder from a_anchor's own side and b_far_shoulder from b_anchor's own side, but then assigns them backwards: actor_a's HandTarget gets target_anchor=b_far_shoulder and actor_b's gets target_anchor=a_far_shoulder. With a_anchor='r_hand', b_anchor='l_hand', actor_a's right hand ends up targeting actor_b's near/same-side shoulder instead of the intended far/crossed shoulder, producing an anatomically wrong or self-intersecting embrace. Invisible with default args (a_anchor==b_anchor=='r_hand') which is all the current test covers.
acceptance_criteria: build_hug_recipe with mismatched anchors (e.g. a_anchor='r_hand', b_anchor='l_hand') produces a correctly crossed embrace; add a test case covering mismatched anchors.
close_reason: Swapped the far-shoulder assignment so each actor's hand target derives from its own anchor side; added a mismatched-anchor regression test and CHANGELOG entry.

title: DPB: zip extraction hardening for plugin installs
description: Harden the drag-and-drop plugin zip installer against path traversal (zip-slip), symlink entries, and zip-bomb resource exhaustion, since archives are effectively untrusted input dropped by the user. Originally flagged as a spec gap with no defenses specified.
design: Vendor miniz (single-header, MIT) matching the project existing cpp-httplib vendoring style -- no QuaZip or libarchive. Reject any entry with an absolute path, a double-dot segment, or a symlink attribute. Enforce max total uncompressed size, max entry count, and per-entry compression-ratio caps, checked live during decompression, not just trusted from header fields, so a crafted archive cannot lie about its size. Extract to a staging dir, validate manifest.json there, and only atomically rename into the final plugin dir once fully validated -- the live plugins dir never contains a partially-extracted or rejected archive. Note: this defends the filesystem, not against a malicious plugin actual Python code -- arbitrary code execution is inherent to running a third-party plugin and is a separate trust-model concern for community distribution, not solved by extraction hardening.
acceptance_criteria: Archives with path-traversal entries, symlink entries, or oversized/bomb content are rejected before or during extraction with no writes outside the staging dir; valid archives land atomically in the final plugin dir.
close_reason: Dead duplicate from an incomplete migration -- real completed copy is daz-python-bridge-sop.3 (closed).

title: Investigate DzScript::hasInclude() heap corruption crash on script.reset()
description:
While running the full tests.py api suite (72 tests) against a live DAZ Studio 4 instance, the app crashed with ACCESS_VIOLATION in ntdll!RtlFreeHeap, called via MSVCR100.dll!free <- dzcore.dll!DzScript::hasInclude <- dzcore.dll!DzScript::~DzScript <- DazScriptServer.dll!DzScriptServerPane::handleExecuteRequest (script.reset() at DzScriptServerPane.cpp:1509).

This is a heap-corruption AV inside dzcore.dll's own DzScript destructor, freeing via the OLD Qt4-bundled CRT (MSVCR100). Matches the documented CRT-heap-mismatch bug class already known in this project (see memory: never store std::string from toStdString() in DazScriptServer structures). The triggering code path (handleExecuteRequest's SDK4 execute()/result() logic) is unchanged from before this session's SDK6 work - likely a pre-existing latent bug, never triggered before because nobody ran this thorough an automated stress test against a live instance.

Need to:
1. Bisect which specific test/script triggers it (heap corruption AVs often manifest later than the actual corrupting call, so the trigger may not be the test immediately preceding the crash).
2. Determine if this reproduces on DAZ Studio 6 (SDK6) too, or is SDK4/dzcore-version-specific.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED. Via live cdb debugging (sxe -c "kb;..." bpe breakpoint-exception filter, since dzcore's RtlReportCriticalFailure delivers a raw int3, not a structured 0xc0000374 SEH exception), captured two distinct heap-corruption stack traces in dzcore.dll, both triggered by completely normal DzScript usage:
1) Fresh-DzScript-per-request pattern: corrupts in dzcore!DzScript::hasInclude <- ~DzScript (called via our script.reset()/destructor).
2) Switched to a persistent/reused DzScript instance (setReuseInterpreter(true)) to avoid #1 -> corruption MOVED to dzcore!DzScriptContext::setArgs <- DzScript::doExecute <- DzScript::execute(args), triggered by repeatedly calling execute(args) on the same reused context.
FIX: keep the persistent/reused DzScript instance (avoids #1), AND avoid execute(args) entirely by injecting args via a getArguments() JS shim (same technique already used for SDK6, where execute(args)+result() never worked at all) then calling the no-arg execute() (avoids #2, since the no-arg path never touches DzScriptContext::setArgs).
VERIFIED: 6 consecutive full 72-test runs (432 total executions) against live DS4 with cdb attached and monitoring for breakpoint exceptions - zero crashes, zero heap-corruption events captured (previously crashed reliably within 1-2 runs). Also lazily construct the persistent DzScript (on first request) rather than in the pane constructor, since eager construction at pane-construction time (which runs very early during DAZ Studio's own startup/pane-restoration) caused a separate immediate startup crash.
Both dzcore.dll bugs (hasInclude/~DzScript and DzScriptContext::setArgs) are real, reproducible, closed-source bugs in DAZ Studio 4's dzcore.dll - confirmed they exist on v2.5.0 too (same dzcore.dll, unrelated to our SDK6 session's code changes), but our specific USAGE PATTERN (constructing per-request scripts, or passing args via execute(args)) is what exercises them. Worth reporting to Daz3D with this exact reproduction info if there's a support channel.
close_reason: Root-caused two distinct dzcore.dll heap-corruption bugs via live debugging; fixed by combining persistent/reused DzScript (lazily constructed) with a getArguments() JS shim to avoid DzScriptContext::setArgs entirely. Verified stable across 6 consecutive full 72-test runs with debugger monitoring confirming zero corruption events.

title: dazpy viewport snapshot API (_viewport.py)
description:
Add a viewport capture method to the dazpy SDK so Python scripts can save the active DAZ Studio 3D viewport to a PNG/JPEG file without triggering a full iRay render.

## Why
The ComfyUI pipeline needs a fast source image. iRay renders take minutes; the OpenGL viewport preview takes under a second. dazpy currently has no way to capture the viewport — only full renders via _render.py. This is also generally useful for thumbnailing, scene inspection, and live preview workflows.

## What needs to be done
- Create dazpy/_viewport.py with a DazViewport class
- capture(path, width=None, height=None) method using DzViewport::captureToFile() via DazScript:
  MainWindow.getViewportMgr().getActiveViewport().get3DViewport().captureToFile(path)
- Optional: set_size(w, h) / get_size() using DzViewport geometry
- Add DazViewport to dazpy/__init__.py exports
- Add unit tests (mock-based) in tests_dazpy.py
- Add integration tests (gated @skip_no_daz) in tests_dazpy_integration.py

## Design decisions
- Use captureToFile() not grabFramebuffer() — captureToFile writes to disk directly, simpler path
- Return the output path as a string for confirmation
- Accept optional width/height to temporarily resize the viewport before capture (restore after)

## Acceptance criteria
- dazpy.DazViewport().capture('C:/tmp/snap.png') writes a valid PNG to disk
- Unit tests pass without a live server
- Integration test passes against a running DAZ Studio instance
notes: DAZ API path: MainWindow.getViewportMgr().getActiveViewport().get3DViewport() returns a Dz3DViewport. The captureToFile(path) method exists on Dz3DViewport. Verify exact method signature with mcp__daz-api__get_class_details('Dz3DViewport') before implementing.
close_reason: Implemented dazpy/_viewport.py with DazViewport.capture(), get_size(), set_size(), is_available(). Exported from __init__.py. 7 unit tests + 4 integration tests added.

title: DAZ-to-ComfyUI img2img enhancement pipeline

## Why
DAZ Studio produces convincing 3D scenes but iRay renders are slow (minutes). The viewport OpenGL preview is fast but low quality. This pipeline bridges the gap: capture the viewport in seconds, then let ComfyUI upscale and photoreal-enhance it with a diffusion model — giving a high-quality result in under a minute without waiting for iRay.

- ComfyUI client, file watcher, workflow template, orchestrator, tests

## Acceptance criteria

title: Fix body_measurements.py: dead torso-loop selector and robust-max never called
description:
Two dead functions exist in body_measurements.py but are never wired into the measurement pipeline, causing significant measurement errors (e.g. bust reported as 157.8 cm instead of ~90 cm):

1. _select_torso_loop() is defined to pick the loop whose centroid is closest to the body centerline (filters out arm cross-sections) but _section_perimeter() calls _best_loop_perimeter() instead, which just picks the largest loop.

2. _robust_profile_max() is defined to reject outlier slices (values > 1.35x median) but _scan_calibrated_band() never calls it; for fallback_mode='max' it just calls max(), which picks the shoulder-area arm-inflated slice.

Fix: wire both functions into the pipeline.
close_reason: Both dead functions wired into pipeline: _select_torso_loop in _section_perimeter, _robust_profile_max in _scan_calibrated_band

title: Add POST /render endpoint (single render, async)
description:
VN production workflows need to trigger DAZ renders programmatically. Without a render endpoint, every render requires manual GUI interaction, making batch sprite production impossible to automate.

Implement POST /render that accepts a render job, enqueues it through the existing AsyncRequestManager, executes on the main thread, and returns a request_id immediately.

Request body schema:
- output_path (required, absolute path)
- width / height (optional, override scene render settings)
- format: png|jpg|tiff|exr (optional, inferred from output_path extension)
- camera (optional, null = active camera)
- engine (optional, null = scene default: iray|3delight|filament)
- figure / morphs (optional, single-figure morph dict)
- figures (optional, list of {name, morphs} for multi-figure scenes)
- iray_samples (optional quality override)

Render jobs use id prefix 'rnd-' and flow through the existing processNextAsyncRequest() path as a special request type. The server generates a DazScript snippet from the morph dict, applies morphs via findPropertyByLabel(), then calls App.getRenderMgr().render(opts). Unknown morph names are silently skipped (non-fatal). Status/result polling via existing /requests/:id/status and /requests/:id/result endpoints.

Open questions to resolve during implementation:
1. morph reset between variants (reset_morphs flag needed?)
2. Figure lookup fallback: error vs fall back to primary figure
3. Add isRender flag to AsyncRequest struct in AsyncRequestManager.h
design:
1. reset_morphs flag: Add reset_morphs: bool to POST /render request body. When true, reset all figure morphs to zero on the main thread before applying the morphs dict and rendering. Required for correct variant rendering when the same figure is reused across batch jobs.

2. Figure lookup failure = error: On figure lookup failure, return an HTTP error (not a silent fallback). Before any render step begins, run a validation pass over the entire figures array to identify all figure references and validate they resolve to scene nodes. This surfaces all bad references at once rather than failing mid-render.

3. RequestType enum instead of isRender bool: Add RequestType enum (REQUEST_TYPE_SCRIPT, REQUEST_TYPE_RENDER) to AsyncRequest struct rather than a boolean isRender flag. Thread it through submit() or a new submitRender() overload. Used in two places: (a) cancelJson() — only invoke killRenderOnMainThread() when cancelling a render request, not any running request; (b) processNextAsyncRequest() — gate render-progress signal wiring for future SSE progress endpoint (owd).
notes:
Implementation complete and tested (2026-05-21). Build clean, installed, verified via live DAZ Studio instance.

- Image size: new QSize(w, h) — NOT Qt.size() (Qt global undefined in DAZ QScriptEngine)
- Engine switching: renderMgr.findRenderer(className) + setActiveRenderer() confirmed working. Iray className = 'DzIrayRenderer'. 3Delight/Filament class names follow Dz*Renderer pattern but need verification on systems with those plugins.
- Camera: Scene.findCameraByLabel() + App.getViewportMgr().setActiveCamera() confirmed.
- Render: renderMgr.doRender(opts) confirmed.
- Output path: opts.renderImgFilename + opts.renderImgToId = 2 (DirectToFile) confirmed.

Needs further investigation — scene data items path not yet found. Resume investigation in a future session.

title: Render job whose script returns success:false (not cancelled) is marked completed
description: Found while fixing alaz. markCompleted() treats a render script returning {success:false} as cancelled only when a cancel was requested; otherwise status is 'completed' and processNextAsyncRequest() emits the SSE 'complete' event. Cases: buildRenderScript pre-flight 'Figure not found' returns {success:false,error}, and renderFinished(false) without a client cancel (e.g. user stops it in the Studio UI). Expected: status failed, SCRIPT_ERROR (or JOB_CANCELLED for a UI cancel?), SSE 'error' event with the script's error text. See src/AsyncRequestManager.cpp markCompleted renderAborted.
close_reason: markCompleted marks a render returning success:false without client cancel as FAILED (SCRIPT_ERROR); processNextAsyncRequest sends SSE error. Live-verified DS6 6.26 via UI cancel of an Iray render; ratchet test added.

title: Server: /render/batch partial-accept 503 is marked retryable
description: src/DzScriptServerPane.cpp (render batch submit, 'Queue full after accepting N of M variants'): returns 503 SERVER_UNAVAILABLE with retryable=true after some variants were already enqueued. That breaks the ErrorResponse contract (retryable = an identical retry may succeed without the client changing anything): an identical resubmit duplicates the accepted variants. dazpy works around it (render_batch_submit passes retry_server_errors=False, yau7.6.3). Fix: a distinct non-retryable code (e.g. BATCH_PARTIALLY_ACCEPTED) whose body lists the accepted request_ids, or roll back the accepted variants; update openapi.yaml, daz-ts and dazpy.
close_reason: Closed

title: Interaction IK: second actor's hand (hug/kiss) and foot strikes don't converge live
description: Live DS6 6.26, 2 x Genesis 9 from rest pose (daz-ts/test/integration/interaction.integration.test.ts, maxIterations 120): every first-actor hand target converges (touch/hug/kiss A r_hand 34.96->0.12 cm, punch 53.54->0.13, handshake B 15.17->0.14). title: Anchor-to-anchor targets aim at bone joint centres, so contact recipes push hands inside the partner's body
description: Live DS6 2026-11-22 (after 6r3b): build_touch_recipe-style HandTarget(A r_hand -> B l_shoulder) converges to 0.95 cm of B's l_shoulder anchor, but that point is the joint centre inside B's torso; A's fingers visibly come out through B's upper chest. Anchor world-point hints (anchor_world_point_hint / anchorWorldPointHint) and the hand's own effector bone are both joint centres, so every contact recipe (touch, handshake, hug, kiss, fight strike) penetrates. Needs a surface offset: e.g. per-anchor outward offsets (shoulder top/outside, chest front), or recipe builders supplying offsets in the target figure's frame, plus a palm/fingertip effector offset. Fix before 5C exposes recipes via DazScene.applyInteractionRecipe. Applies to dazpy and daz-ts.
close_reason: Shoulder/knee anchors now use the upper-arm/shin joints (G9 l_shoulder is the clavicle). Anchor-to-anchor targets resolve a surface_standoff (target body radius + effector hand/foot reach from descendant bones; half a hand for hand-to-hand), staged in build_pose_patch and applied at alignment along the horizontal approach to the source limb root. Live DS6 2xG9 touch: converged 0.15 cm in 89 iters, wrist 21.1 cm from B's shoulder joint, nearest finger joint 10.5 cm (was fingers through B's chest).

title: Interaction pose patch stages every figure at the origin on live scenes (local_position is always zero)
description: build_pose_patch (dazpy _interaction.py) / buildPosePatch (daz-ts interactionPlan.ts) stage figures from BoneProfile.local_position. Live boneMetadata() and sceneSnapshot() report local_position {0,0,0} for every bone (all 138 on Genesis 9, DS4 4.24 and DS6, 2026-11-22), so every figure is staged at [0,0,0]; a two-figure touch recipe leaves both figures overlapping. The hand IK then can't reach the partner's shoulder (40 iterations, error 65.8 -> 39.2). Unit tests miss it because their fixtures set local_position by hand. Fix: stage from world_position relative to the figure's own world position (or have boneMetadata return a figure-relative offset), in both SDKs, and add a live check. Blocks a useful DazScene.applyInteractionRecipe (sf7y.3).
close_reason: Staging uses world_position - figure_position offsets, floor-locked for hand/foot targets; IK targets shifted by staging displacement. Live-verified DS6 touch recipe.
