title: Script server leaks active_requests slots until CONCURRENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED
description: 2026-11-17: after a blanket pytest run against DS4 (plugin 2.12.0; most integration tests got HTTP 401 because no token was set), /health showed active_requests=10 (the concurrency limit) with no client connected, and every request, even 'return 1+1', got CONCURRENT_LIMIT_EXCEEDED until the server was restarted. Netstat showed 3 Studio sockets in CLOSE_WAIT. Suspects: a 401/early-return or client-disconnect path (SSE stream, long-poll ?wait=true) that increments the active counter but never decrements it. Reproduce with targeted requests (not the test suite): unauthenticated requests per route, then clients disconnecting mid long-poll/SSE, checking active_requests after each.
acceptance_criteria: Root cause found; active_requests returns to 0 after every failure/disconnect path; a regression test covers it.
notes: Investigation 2026-11-19: counter is RAII (ActiveRequestSlot, DzScriptServerPane.cpp:936), taken only by sync POST /execute and /scripts/:id/execute; every early return (401/429/400) releases it. It cannot leak — it stays held only while a handler thread is still inside. Sync handlers call the main thread with BlockingQueuedConnection and NO timeout (RequestHandlers.cpp ExecuteScriptHandler/ScriptExecuteHandler). Hypothesis: on 11-17, dazpy integration tests (dazpy reads the token file, so they ran; known to freeze Studio) blocked the main thread; later sync executes piled up behind it in BlockingQueuedConnection → 10 slots held → 429 for everything; clients timed out → CLOSE_WAIT. Respond-if-busy gate only covers scene load/save/clear/render, not a long or stuck script. Safe live repro: 1 sync execute with ~20s busy loop, then 12 sync executes with 2s client timeout; expect active_requests=10 + 429 until the loop ends. Proposed fix: replace the blocking crossing with queued call + shared state (PENDING/RUNNING/ABANDONED, CAS); worker waits in slices, abandons while PENDING on deadline or req.is_connection_closed() → 503 STUDIO_BUSY retryable; main thread skips abandoned calls.
close_reason: Root cause: sync execute crossed to main thread with BlockingQueuedConnection (no timeout); queued requests behind a busy/stuck main thread held ActiveRequestSlots forever, even after client disconnect. Counter itself never leaked. Fix: MainThreadCall (queued + CAS abandon on client disconnect / server timeout -> 503 STUDIO_BUSY, never runs). Regression test TestConcurrency.test_disconnected_queued_requests_release_their_slots (red on old build: 7 slots held; green on DS4 + DS6). Commit 628a4f7.

title: daz-ts: publish to npm (@bluemoonfoundry/daz-ts) via trusted publishing
description:
daz-ts is built and attached to GitHub releases as a tarball only. npm can't install a package from a git-repo subdirectory, so the only install route is the release-asset URL (no semver ranges, no npm update, can't be a dependency of other packages). Publish to the public npm registry, the equivalent of dazpy's PyPI publishing. Supersedes the design spec's "not published to public npm" decision (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-06-daz-ts-design.md) - update the spec.

Plan:
- Name: @bluemoonfoundry/daz-ts (scoped; both it and unscoped daz-ts were free on 2026-11-18). Reserve early.
- Own release train: tag daz-ts-v<version> with its own publish workflow, since daz-ts versions independently (0.1.0) and npm publish has no skip-existing - publishing on every plugin tag would fail when daz-ts isn't bumped. Alternative: guard with npm view <name>@<version>.
- Trusted publishing (OIDC): publish job needs permissions id-token: write and npm CLI >= 11.5.1; provenance is automatic. Configure the trusted publisher (repo + workflow file) on npmjs.com - requires the user's npm account/org.
- package.json: rename, add repository (must match the GitHub repo for provenance), exports map, publishConfig.access public.
- Version check for daz-ts (tag vs package.json), analogous to scripts/check_version_consistency.py.
- Keep the .tgz on GitHub releases.
- Optional: TypeDoc API docs alongside dazpy's Sphinx docs.
acceptance_criteria: A daz-ts-v* tag publishes @bluemoonfoundry/daz-ts to npmjs.com with provenance from GitHub Actions (no long-lived token); npm install @bluemoonfoundry/daz-ts works in a clean project; plugin v* releases still succeed without a daz-ts bump; design spec updated.
notes:
Repo side done 2026-11-20: package renamed @bluemoonfoundry/daz-ts (exports, repository, publishConfig.access), publish-daz-ts.yml on daz-ts-v* tags (OIDC trusted publishing, skip-if-exists, GH release not-latest), scripts/check_daz_ts_version.py (+CI, tests), docs/spec/changelog. Remaining (user): manual first npm publish from bluemoonfoundry account, then configure trusted publisher (repo daz-script-server, workflow publish-daz-ts.yml), then push daz-ts-v0.1.0 tag to verify the workflow. Close after that.
2026-11-23: 0.1.0 is on npm (hand-published 2026-11-20, no provenance); the daz-ts-v0.1.0 workflow run skipped publish because the version already existed, so the OIDC trusted-publishing path is still unverified. Trusted publisher IS configured on npmjs.com. DECISION: no 0.1.1 test release. Verify with daz-ts 0.2.0, cut together with minor bumps of the plugin and dazpy once outstanding work is done (one joint release). Close when daz-ts-v0.2.0 publishes with dist.attestations. Also pending (needs npm login): npm deprecate @bluemoonfoundry/daz-ts@0.0.0-stage 'Placeholder, not a real release. Use 0.1.x or later.'
close_reason: daz-ts-v0.2.0 published @bluemoonfoundry/daz-ts@0.2.0 via OIDC trusted publishing with SLSA provenance (run 45330471562); clean-project install + npm audit signatures verified. Needed: ./ tarball path fix (#70) and re-creating the expired trusted publisher (npm trust github). 0.0.0-stage deprecation filed separately.

title: pinocchio-ik native crash in configuration_from_angles blocks test validation
description:
## Context
While validating daz-script-server-hb5t.3 (finger IK wrist-frame-correction fix), running test_finger_ik.py against the pinocchio-ik conda env (X:\apps\miniforge3\envs\pinocchio-ik) crashes with 'Windows fatal exception: code 0xc06d007f' (native access violation, not a Python exception) whenever a test calls pinocchio_ik.configuration_from_angles() -> bone_local_rotation() -> _compose_euler() (pinocchio_ik.py line 128).

## Reproduction
Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to the hb5t.3 diff: stashing the uncommitted finger_ik.py/hand_landmarks.py/test_finger_ik.py changes and re-running the OLD (already-committed) test_solve_digit_chain_recovers_known_tip_hinge_angle test crashes identically. So this affects the already-merged pinocchio_ik.py/finger_ik.py test suite too, not just new code.

## Likely cause
0xc06d007f smells like a native DLL/runtime conflict (e.g. numpy's bundled OpenBLAS vs. Pinocchio's own Eigen/BLAS linkage on Windows conda-forge), not a logic bug in _compose_euler itself -- the axis-rotation math there is simple numpy.

## Impact
Cannot currently get a green pytest run for anything that exercises real IK solving (configuration_from_angles) on this machine's pinocchio-ik env. This blocked full validation of hb5t.3's fix, though code review + wiring inspection + the tests that don't hit this path (20/26) passed. Needs investigation before any pinocchio_ik-based feature can be fully test-validated locally.

## Next steps
- Try reproducing outside pytest (bare python -c) to rule out pytest-specific interaction
- Check for numpy/OpenBLAS version pinned in environment.yml vs. what's actually installed in X:\apps\miniforge3\envs\pinocchio-ik
- Consider conda-forge pinocchio + numpy ABI mismatch as prime suspect
close_reason: Not a code bug -- root cause was invoking the pinocchio-ik env's python.exe by raw path instead of through 'conda run'/run_pinocchio.ps1/.sh, which skips PATH setup for the env's Library/bin (numpy BLAS + pinocchio's Eigen/shared libs). Confirmed: running 'conda run -p .../pinocchio-ik python -m pytest test_finger_ik.py' gives a clean 26/26 pass, including the previously-crashing test_solve_digit_chain_recovers_known_tip_hinge_angle and the new wrist-frame regression test. This exact pitfall is already documented in run_pinocchio.ps1's header comment ('a missing DLL on PATH segfaults with no traceback').

title: Facial expression capture/application from image(s)
description:
Add facial expression posing to the batch pipeline: either an explicit expression-extraction pass, or by passing one or more --image paths to extract an expression from and apply while holding body pose and dForce constant.

## Context
User wants to (a) capture facial expression state explicitly and/or (b) pass one or more --image PATH args, extract an expression from each, and apply it to the figure, re-rendering with body pose and dForce results held fixed -- i.e. expression becomes an independent axis on top of the existing photo->body-pose pipeline, potentially many-expressions x one-body-pose (or combined with the existing many-photos batch).

## Current state (checked 2026-09-12) -- least scaffolded of the four subsystems
- dazpy has no expression-specific API. Only a generic DazMorph.value getter/setter (Y:/working/BlueMoonFoundry/daz-script-server/dazpy/_morph.py) -- usable for expression morphs by name/label if found via existing node/property lookup, but nothing purpose-built.
- No face-landmark extraction module exists in daz-script-server-examples -- hand_landmarks.py is the closest analog (wraps MediaPipe HandLandmarker) but there is no equivalent FaceLandmarker wrapper yet. MediaPipe does have a Face Landmarker task (with blendshape/expression output) that would be the natural extraction backend, analogous to how PoseLandmarker/HandLandmarker are used today.
- Genesis 9 supports facial expression via both ERC-driven expression morphs (viseme/emotion presets) AND/OR facial bones -- unclear yet which representation the pipeline should target; needs research (similar to how the body-IK work had to discover bone_metadata()/rotation_order/rest_orientation details before building the Pinocchio model).
- No existing 'hold X constant while updating Y' pattern in the codebase yet -- the --fingers flag is the closest precedent (runs after body IK, additive) but expression-only re-render (keep pose/dforce, only touch expression) is a new interaction shape.

## Open questions for the design pass
- Scope for v1: expression-only morphs (probably simpler, matches 'extraction pass' framing) vs. facial bone-driven expression (more expressive but a much bigger lift, closer to the existing body IK complexity). Recommend starting with expression morphs/blendshapes given MediaPipe FaceLandmarker's native blendshape output maps naturally to that.
- 'Explicit expression extraction pass' vs. 'multiple --image' -- are these two separate features or one (extraction pass = the mechanism, --image = the CLI entry point to it)? Needs to be disambiguated with the user; issue title currently treats them as one.
- Multi-image handling: does each --image produce a separate expression variant re-rendered against the SAME already-solved body pose (expression x existing photo batch), or is this a standalone mode unrelated to --batch? This determines whether it's additive to the existing batch loop or a new CLI mode.
- Given this is the least scaffolded subsystem, likely needs its own spike/research step (confirm MediaPipe FaceLandmarker blendshape output + Genesis 9's actual expression morph/property names live against DAZ Studio) before a full design can be written -- flag this as probably the first sub-task when this issue is picked up.
- Likely the largest of the four and may itself need decomposing further once scoped (e.g. separate issues for 'add FaceLandmarker extraction module' vs. 'wire expression into the batch pipeline' vs. 'dazpy expression API additions').
close_reason: Implemented --expression-image in pose_transfer_photo.py: MediaPipe FaceLandmarker blendshapes -> Genesis 9 facs_bs_*/facs_ctrl_* morphs, see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-13-expression-capture-design.md and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-13-expression-capture.md. title: Fix finger-posing coordinate misalignment: MediaPipe Hand/Pose landmark conventions don't share a rotation frame
description:
## Context

daz-script-server-examples/ai_vision/pose_transfer_photo/'s new --fingers
flag (design spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-finger-posing-design.md
in that repo) assumed MediaPipe's Pose Landmarker and Hand Landmarker world
landmarks share a rotational axis convention, differing only in their
translation origin -- finger_ik.anchor_hand_landmarks() implements this as a
pure translation (apply the body pipeline's existing scale+rotation
transform, then translate the whole 21-landmark set so the wrist landmark
lands on the already-solved l_hand/r_hand world position). The spec called
this out explicitly as an assumption to verify live, with a staged fallback
plan if wrong.

## What was found (live validation, 2026-09-10)

Ran --fingers --backend pinocchio against DAZ Studio ("Jason Cross",
d:/ghirp/Downloaded Content/body2.png, one hand detected: "Left"). Result:
FALSIFIED. l_index2, l_mid2, l_ring2 (PIP joints) and l_index3 all landed
pinned exactly at the POSITIVE (hyperextension) boundary of their axis_limits
range, while the source photo clearly shows that hand's fingers curled
INWARD (flexion = negative z per finger_ik.py's convention). Per-digit
convergence errors were 3.6-11.3 scene units (one to two orders of magnitude
worse than the body limb residuals of 0.003-0.15), with several digits
settling into a 2-value oscillating limit cycle -- the solver repeatedly
hitting a joint-limit boundary and bouncing off it, meaning the unconstrained
target it wants lies outside the physically reachable range entirely. This
is the "wrong direction" failure mode the spec's own fallback plan
anticipated, not ordinary IK residual (magnitude-only shortfall with correct
sign).

Full findings, bone-by-bone rotation table, and photo comparison:
Y:/working/BlueMoonFoundry/daz-script-server-examples/.superpowers/sdd/2026-09-10-finger-posing/task-7-report.md
(this is a session-scratch directory that may get cleaned up -- the
essential findings are captured in this issue's description and design
notes below; recover full detail from git history / that report if it still
exists, or re-run the live validation).

## Recommended fix (per the spec's own fallback plan)

Per-hand Kabsch/Procrustes rotation alignment: using WRIST + INDEX_MCP +
PINKY_MCP as a stable corresponding triangle, compute a best-fit rotation
between MediaPipe's raw hand landmarks and the DAZ rig's own rest-pose hand
geometry, and apply that rotation (not just a translation) when anchoring
hand landmarks to the solved wrist position. This changes
finger_ik.anchor_hand_landmarks() from a pure translation into a
translation+rotation.

This is real new algorithmic work (SVD-based rotation fitting), not a
sign-flip guess -- it needs its own brainstorming pass before implementation,
per the design spec's explicit guidance on this fallback.

## Related work

- Design spec: daz-script-server-examples/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-10-finger-posing-design.md
- Implementation plan (Tasks 1-7, all complete and reviewed clean):
  daz-script-server-examples/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-10-finger-posing.md
- The IK/chain-solving machinery itself (finger_ik.py, reusing pinocchio_ik.py's
  active-set solver) is verified correct and does NOT need to change -- only
  the landmark-to-world-space anchoring step.
notes:
LIVE RE-VALIDATION COMPLETE (2026-09-12), now that daz-script-server-9825 is
fixed: re-ran `pose_transfer_photo.py --backend pinocchio --fingers --figure
"Jason Cross" d:/ghirp/Downloaded Content/body2.png --debug` against live
DAZ Studio (zero_figure() applied first per script precondition).

RESULT: CONFIRMED FIXED. Compared applied bone rotations against
bone_metadata() axis_limits directly:
- Before (original bug): l_index2/l_mid2/l_ring2 pinned at the POSITIVE
  (hyperextension) z-axis boundary, 2-value oscillating limit cycles,
  per-digit errors 3.6-11.3 scene units.
- After (Kabsch fix): r_index2/r_mid2/r_ring2/r_pinky2 now settle at z=-12,
  the FLEXION (minimum) boundary -- correct direction for the photo's
  curled-fingers pose -- with stable convergence (no oscillation) and
  per-digit errors down to 1.5-3.5 scene units. r_thumb1/r_thumb3 also
  settled into flexion-direction values (x=-15 flexion limit, z=-20 flexion
  limit).

Digits still report NOT CONVERGED against the tolerance threshold (they're
hitting real anatomical joint-limit boundaries, likely because the photo's
apparent finger curl exceeds MediaPipe-landmark-implied targets translated
through this rig's specific limit ranges) -- that's a residual-magnitude/
reachability question, not a correctness bug, and is out of scope for this
issue (which was specifically about the wrong-direction anchoring assumption
falsified in the original report). Closing as fixed.
close_reason: Kabsch rotation fix confirmed correct via live re-validation: fingers now flex in the correct (photo-matching) direction instead of pinning at the wrong hyperextension boundary. Residual convergence gap against joint limits is a separate reachability concern, not a correctness bug.

title: Pinocchio-based batch IK solver for pose_transfer_photo (many photos x many figures)
description:
## Context

daz-script-server-examples/ai_vision/pose_transfer_photo/pose_transfer_photo.py
extracts a body pose from a photo (MediaPipe PoseLandmarker) and drives a
Genesis 9 figure's hands/feet toward the photo-derived positions. It currently
uses a custom stacked-Jacobian multi-effector IK solve, implemented entirely
via raw DazScript HTTP calls to DAZ Studio: ~150 iterations, each iteration =
1 HTTP round-trip to DAZ Studio's main thread (build Jacobian server-side,
apply delta, repeat). This works and produces good results (verified live:
head upright, arms/legs naturally posed, matching a reference photo) but is
slow (~10-30s per pose) because the numerical solve itself is bottlenecked on
network round-trips, not on the actual linear algebra.

User wants to scale this to **many photos x many figures** (batch processing).
At that scale the round-trip-per-iteration cost dominates badly.

## Decision from prior session

Move the IK solve off DAZ Studio's main thread entirely using Pinocchio (C++
rigid-body dynamics library, Python bindings) for local forward-kinematics +
Jacobian computation:

- **Once per unique figure** (not per photo): read `bone_metadata()` (bone
  hierarchy, rest local_position offsets, rotation_order -- same data
  pose_transfer_photo.py already pulls for calibration) and build a Pinocchio
  kinematic model dynamically from it. Genesis 9 figures share rig *topology*
  (same bone hierarchy/rotation order) but differ in *proportions* (arm/leg
  length from body-shape morphs) -- so this can't be a single static URDF
  file; it must be built (or at least scaled) per figure from live data, then
  cached.
- **Per photo**: MediaPipe extraction + target calibration stay exactly as
  implemented today (no changes needed there). The IK solve itself runs
  entirely in Pinocchio locally -- no HTTP round-trips during iteration --
  then exactly one `set_bone_rotations()` call pushes the final joint angles
  to DAZ Studio.
- This collapses the HTTP cost from (photos x figures x ~150 iterations) to
  (photos x figures) -- one push each -- plus a one-time model build per
  unique figure (amortized across every photo run against that figure).

## Chain-composition lessons from the current solver (must carry over)

These were hard-won via live debugging in the prior session and directly
apply to the Pinocchio model too -- don't rediscover them:

- Exclude `spine4` from hand IK chains: it's the *only* extra reach dazpy's
  own auto-selected hand_to_target() chain has beyond the forearm, and an
  underdetermined solver will use it freely, wrenching the spine to hit a
  wrist target with zero position error but a wrong-looking pose.
- Exclude `hip` from leg IK chains: it's the skeleton's actual root
  (parent=None; even spine1 is its child), so letting a foot-reach solve
  rotate it tips the *entire* body -- torso, arms, head -- to gain a little
  leg reach. Root leg chains at `pelvis` instead (a *sibling* of spine1, not
  its ancestor) -- structurally cannot touch the spine.
- Current chains (see `_CHAINS` in pose_transfer_photo.py):
  `l_hand: [l_shoulder, l_upperarm, l_forearm]`,
  `r_hand: [r_shoulder, r_upperarm, r_forearm]`,
  `l_foot: [pelvis, l_thigh, l_shin]`,
  `r_foot: [pelvis, r_thigh, r_shin]`.
- A pure position-target DLS solve on an underdetermined system (many joint
  DOFs, few effector constraints) needs a rest-pose bias (null-space
  secondary objective, or Pinocchio's equivalent) or it converges to
  anatomically-odd-but-zero-error solutions. Current script's
  `--rest-pose-weight` (default 0.15) does this via null-space projection --
  Pinocchio will need an equivalent regularization term.

## First step (do this before building the full batch pipeline)

**Validation, not implementation first.** Get Pinocchio installed (flag
Windows install friction early -- it's a compiled C++/Eigen dependency,
historically fiddly on Windows per earlier research this session, which found
zero existing pinocchio/scipy/ikpy usage anywhere in dazpy despite a stubbed
`SolveOptions.backend` field). Build a kinematic model for ONE figure/chain
from live `bone_metadata()`, and confirm Pinocchio's forward-kinematics output
for that model matches DAZ Studio's actual bone world-positions
(`getWSPos()` via bone_metadata()) before trusting any solve built on it. A
subtle rotation-order or offset mistake in the model-building code would not
necessarily be obvious downstream.

## Known constraints / environment

- DAZ Studio 2.9.2 is the live test target (127.0.0.1:18811, DazScriptServer
  plugin). Figure used for testing: "Jason Cross" (Genesis 9).
- `dazpy.poses.zero_figure(figure)` must be called before each pose-transfer
  test run -- calibration reads the figure's *current* pose.
- Separately (unrelated bug, already filed): daz-script-server-jbnq --
  `DazScene.undo_last()` throws `App.getUndoStack is not a function` against
  this DAZ Studio build. Not blocking for this work (the example already uses
  `scene.undo()` context-manager style, not `undo_last()`), but worth knowing
  if debugging live state gets messy.
- Test images used previously: d:/ghirp/Downloaded Content/body2.png (single
  person, standing, good input) -- d:/ghirp/Downloaded Content/body1.webp was
  discovered to be an 8-person reference mood board, NOT a valid single-pose
  input (MediaPipe silently locks onto one panel).

## Files

- Y:\working\BlueMoonFoundry\daz-script-server-examples\ai_vision\pose_transfer_photo\pose_transfer_photo.py
  -- current stacked-Jacobian implementation (keep working as a fallback /
  reference; the Pinocchio path could be a new script or a flag on this one).
- Y:\working\BlueMoonFoundry\daz-script-server-examples\ai_vision\pose_transfer_photo\README.md
  -- documents current architecture and the chain-composition reasoning above
  in more detail.
- Y:\working\BlueMoonFoundry\daz-script-server\dazpy\_interaction.py -- has
  the stubbed `SolveOptions.backend: Literal["scipy","pinocchio","ikpy","auto"]`
  field (unused, no dispatch logic) and `FigureRigProfile`/`BoneProfile`
  dataclasses that already model bone hierarchy + rest positions in a
  solver-friendly shape -- worth checking whether these can be reused/extended
  as the Pinocchio model-building input instead of writing that from scratch.
notes:
## Env reconciliation: environment.yml + wrapper scripts + friendly import error (2026-09-12, same session)

User asked: since Pinocchio only installs via a separate conda-forge env
(x:/apps/miniforge3/envs/pinocchio-ik) distinct from the default mediapipe
venv, should that be documented in the README or handled some more
automated way? Landed on: don't automate env CREATION (installing a
compiled C++/Eigen toolchain is a heavy one-time action that should stay a
conscious user step), but DO automate env RESOLUTION/invocation, since
that's the part that actually caused friction this session (guessing the
right interpreter + manually prepending Library/bin to PATH for numpy's
BLAS DLL).

Added:
- environment.yml (pose_transfer_photo/): pins to what's actually
  installed and live-validated in pinocchio-ik (python 3.12.14, pinocchio
  4.1.0, numpy 2.5.3, scipy 1.18.0 via conda-forge; mediapipe 1.0.1,
  opencv-python 5.0.0.93 via pip) rather than the stale python=3.11 the old
  docstring suggested. Also pip-installs dazpy editable from a relative
  sibling-repo path, with a documented fallback (`pip install dazpy`) if
  someone's clone layout doesn't have daz-script-server-examples and
  daz-script-server as siblings.
- run_pinocchio.ps1 / run_pinocchio.sh: thin wrappers around `conda run -n
  pinocchio-ik --no-capture-output`, which (confirmed live) sets up
  PATH/DLL resolution correctly by itself -- no manual Library/bin
  prepending needed, matching the module docstring's own long-standing
  recommendation that nothing before this session actually implemented.
  Both resolve `conda` from PATH first, else $env:PINOCCHIO_IK_CONDA_ROOT /
  $PINOCCHIO_IK_CONDA_ROOT, else a documented default guess; both check the
  env exists first and print the `conda env create` fix if not, before
  attempting to run anything.
- pinocchio_ik.py: `import pinocchio as pin` wrapped in try/except ->
  sys.exit() with copy-pasteable fix-it instructions (which wrapper script
  to use, or manual `conda activate` + `conda env create` if the env is
  missing) instead of a bare ModuleNotFoundError.
- Updated cross-references in pinocchio_ik.py's docstring,
  pose_transfer_photo.py's docstring/--backend help text, and README.md's
  Dependencies/Usage sections to point at environment.yml + the wrapper
  scripts as the one source of truth, replacing the old inline `conda
  create -n pinocchio-ik -c conda-forge python=3.11 ...` instructions that
  had drifted from the actually-installed env.

Live-validated all three end-to-end against DAZ Studio 2.9.2: (1) the
ImportError message triggers correctly and prints working instructions
when run under system python (no pinocchio installed); (2)
run_pinocchio.ps1 correctly resolves conda, confirms the env exists, and
successfully runs both single-photo and --batch modes end-to-end
(single-photo: solved and applied a real pose; --batch: 1-photo batch
reproduced the exact known l_foot=0.152 NOT-CONVERGED baseline, since batch
mode's automatic zero_figure() reset made it directly comparable to the
earlier from-rest validation runs). Exit code 0 in both cases.

This closes out the "environment friction" gap that was previously only a
documented warning (module docstring) rather than something a fresh
contributor could actually follow without live troubleshooting -- same
class of gap as the FigureModel caching layer earlier in this issue (a
docstring claimed behavior that the code/tooling didn't actually provide).

title: dazpy DazScene.undo_last() broken on DAZ Studio 2.9.2: App.getUndoStack is not a function
description: Calling scene.undo_last() (Edit > Undo equivalent) raises ScriptRuntimeError: 'Line 4: TypeError: Result of expression App.getUndoStack [undefined] is not a function' against a live DAZ Studio 2.9.2 instance. Likely an API rename/removal in this Studio version — App.getUndoStack() and the paired redo_last() (App.getUndoStack().redo()) in dazpy/_scene.py need a working replacement or version-guarded fallback. Discovered while testing ai_vision/pose_transfer_photo (daz-script-server-examples) — after a partially-converged IK test, undo_last() could not revert the figure's pose, so it had to be corrected manually via a follow-up hand_to_target call instead of a true undo.
close_reason: Fixed: App.getUndoStack() never existed in the DazScript API; replaced with the global UndoStack object (Global::UndoStack, DzUndoStack class) which is what DAZ Studio actually exposes. title: POST /render/:id/cancel is a no-op on in-flight renders and misreports status (GH #34)
description: AsyncRequestManager::cancelRenderJson() (AsyncRequestManager.cpp:259-314) only sets req.status = REQUEST_CANCELLED when the request is still REQUEST_QUEUED. If the request is already running, it just sets cancelRequested=1 and invokes killRenderOnMainThread() -- but the HTTP response unconditionally returns {"status":"cancelled"} regardless of branch, while the tracker's internal status is left as 'running'. If killRender() finds nothing to kill (e.g. renderer already wedged behind a modal), the request never leaves 'running'. Same bug exists in the non-render cancelJson() path. (GH issue #34, suggestion #3)
acceptance_criteria: After POST /render/:id/cancel (or /requests/:id/cancel) on a running request, GET /requests/:id reflects a terminal status (cancelled or failed) consistent with the cancel response, even when killRender() has nothing to kill.
notes: Live-verified 2026-08-14 against running DAZ Studio 4: submitted a busy-loop script (500M iterations, ~8s, non-render), confirmed it reached RUNNING via poll, then DELETE /requests/:id returned {status:cancelled} and an immediate follow-up GET /requests/:id/status also showed cancelled (not stuck at running) -- the underlying loop kept executing in the background as expected (non-render scripts have no kill mechanism), but the tracker no longer misreports it. Regression test tests/test_api.py::test_async_cancel_running_request_reaches_terminal_status confirmed passing standalone and as part of the cancel/async group.
close_reason: cancelJson()/cancelRenderJson() now mark the request CANCELLED immediately on cancel of a RUNNING request (same as the QUEUED branch), instead of leaving status='running' when killRender() has nothing to kill. Best-effort killRenderOnMainThread() is still invoked for render requests. markCompleted()'s existing terminal-state guard (from the eaub stale-running fix) prevents a late real completion from flipping status back. Added tests/test_api.py::test_async_cancel_running_request_reaches_terminal_status (not live-verified this session — DAZ Studio wasn't running).

title: Fix subtle blacker-than-black halo around head in face-identity pass
description: After the SAM silhouette-masking fix (daz-script-server-7z8), a much subtler artifact remained: a thin halo around the head silhouette that was slightly DARKER than the ambient pure-black background (measured ~[1,1,0] vs ambient ~[5,4,4]), confirmed live via pixel sampling and visually in a zoomed crop. Root cause: even with a true SAM silhouette (not a rectangle), SAMDetectorCombined's own dilation=60 and SEGSPaste's feather=5 were still wide enough to re-encode a thin ring of background pixels through the VAE round-trip during SEGSDetailer's low-denoise pass, and that round-trip produces a near-black that's very slightly darker than the untouched original. Fixed by tightening SAMDetectorCombined's dilation to 10 and SEGSPaste's feather to 2 (bbox_expansion=80, the search hint SAM gets, stays generous since it doesn't directly correspond to the final replaced region). Verified live via precise pixel sampling and full-image visual inspection: residual dip is now a single near-invisible pixel rather than a visible band.

title: SceneSaving busy detection never fires for some save paths
description:
Live testing on feature/studio-busy-handling (through commit 720736f) found that saving to a specific file (2 separate test runs) never fired scene.saving/scene.saved SSE events at all -- confirmed via a live SSE stream capture during the save (push-based, so absence is conclusive, not a timing/polling miss). This means SceneEventBroker::onSceneSaveStarting()/onSceneSaved() are never invoked for this save path, so the SceneSaving busy-tracking branch (enterBusy(MainThreadBusy::SceneSaving)) is currently a no-op for at least this trigger. DzProgress::isActive()/DzBackgroundProgress::isActive() also did not catch a blocking window in either test.

Contrast with scene load (fires reliably, just has a separate trailing-tail gap after sceneLoaded -- see daz-script-server-063) and render (fires cleanly with zero gaps -- aboutToRender/renderFinished bracket the whole operation).

Practical impact is likely smaller than the load case since saves observed were fast (~2s each), but it's a real gap, not just an edge case: any request landing during a save currently has no fast-fail coverage at all, same as pre-fix behavior, for however long the save takes.

Needs investigation: why doesn't DzScene::sceneSaveStarting()/sceneSaved() fire for 'save to a specific file'? Possible causes: this save path may route through a different internal DAZ Studio API than DzScene::saveFile() (e.g. asset/content manager save, or a script-driven save vs UI Save/Save As), or the signal semantics may differ from what was assumed when this feature was designed. Should test other save triggers (Ctrl+S, File > Save, File > Save As with different destinations) to see if any of them do fire the signals, to isolate which specific trigger path is unbracketed.

Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-22-studio-busy-handling-design.md. Plan: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-22-studio-busy-handling.md.
close_reason: Root cause found via code inspection + live test: /scene/save-copy has two branches. The dirty-scene branch calls dzScene->saveScene() and DOES fire sceneSaveStarting/sceneSaved reliably -- confirmed live via a concurrent SSE capture during a real save-copy call against the currently-open (dirty) scene, both the destPath save and the origFilename restore-save fired cleanly. The clean-scene fast path (QFile::copy, src/DzScriptServerPane.cpp ~2931) never calls saveScene() at all, so signals never fire for it -- this fully explains '2/2 test runs never fired', since repeated test runs against an already-saved scene would deterministically hit this branch every time, not flakily. Fixed by making SceneEventBroker::enterBusy()/exitBusy() public and wrapping handleSaveCopy()'s entire body (both branches) in an RAII BusyScope guard, so busy tracking for this handler no longer depends on DzScene's internal signal coverage. Verified: builds cleanly (link step blocked only by the DLL being locked by the currently-running Studio instance -- expected, install requires Studio closed). Live re-verification with the rebuilt DLL still needed next session.

title: Wire DazBusyError into daz-mcp-server's tool error mapping
description: Separate repo: Y:/working/BlueMoonFoundry/daz-mcp-server. Add a case to _errors.py::handle_dazpy_error for daz_exc.DazBusyError (catches both StudioBusyError and ConcurrencyLimitError), raising ToolError(f'DAZ Studio is busy ({exc.reason}). Try again in a few seconds.') so Claude sees a fast, clear signal instead of a multi-minute tool-call hang. No MCP tool should opt into dazpy's retry_on_busy by default -- deliberate, keeps behavior predictable and visible to the LLM. Design: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-22-studio-busy-handling-design.md section 3 (daz-script-server repo). Depends on the dazpy DazBusyError hierarchy shipping (feature/studio-busy-handling branch, commit 89aaafd, Tasks 5-6).
close_reason: Already implemented and merged in the daz-mcp-server repo: PR #4 (feature/studio-busy-handling, merged 2026-07-24) added the DazBusyError case to _errors.py::handle_dazpy_error exactly per this issue's spec, plus a follow-up dazpy>=2.8.0 dependency bump (d4dbe50). Confirmed present on daz-mcp-server's origin/master. Issue was just stale in bd.

title: Manually verify STUDIO_BUSY 503 behavior against live DAZ Studio
description: Task 4 of docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-22-studio-busy-handling.md (branch feature/studio-busy-handling, commit 89aaafd). Install the built plugin, trigger a real scene load and a real render through the DAZ Studio UI, and confirm /execute returns 503 STUDIO_BUSY quickly (not hanging) for the full duration, with a Retry-After header, then returns to normal 200 once idle. Also specifically watch the nesting edge case: hit /execute repeatedly THROUGHOUT a large File>Open (not just once) to confirm no brief 200/hang gap appears mid-load if DAZ nests scene-clear signals inside the load — see beads follow-up for the depth-counter hardening if this is observed.
close_reason: Completed via live testing on feature/studio-busy-handling (commits through 720736f). Confirmed 503 STUDIO_BUSY fires with Retry-After header and correct 'detail' text; confirmed the initially-hypothetical nesting risk (File->Open nests scene.clear_starting/cleared inside scene.loading) was real, fixed with a depth counter; found and partially closed a second gap (trailing node-loading after sceneLoaded() with no covering DzScene signal) by also polling DzProgress/DzBackgroundProgress. Residual small race window at phase boundaries accepted as a known limitation -- see follow-up issue for the bounded-wait backstop that would close it fully.

title: Archive daz-python-bridge once package runner is proven working
description: Once DzPackageImporter + example .dzpkg package are verified working end-to-end in a live DAZ Studio session, add ARCHIVED.md to daz-python-bridge pointing at the new location in daz-script-server, freeze main. Do not delete -- the warm-worker/JSON-RPC design may be worth resurrecting for a different use case later. NEEDS EXPLICIT USER SIGN-OFF before archiving.
close_reason: daz-python-bridge archived: main frozen, ARCHIVED.md added pointing at this repo's Package Runner (epic 5sw, verified end-to-end in a live DAZ Studio session). Not deleted, per plan.

title: ERC-inflation fix in DazPose doesn't cover bone rotation channels
description: dazpy/_pose.py:324 - Commit d279a9a ('stop DazPose/checkpoint round trips from inflating ERC-linked properties') switches morphs and node properties to getRawValue()/setRawValue(), but bone XRotControl/YRotControl/ZRotControl channels are still read/written via plain getValue()/setValue(), unchanged by that commit. For rigs where one bone's rotation channel is ERC-driven from another (e.g. auto-follow bend/twist ratios common on Genesis figures), repeated DazPose capture->apply cycles will keep reading/writing the post-ERC total for that bone, inflating it the same way the commit fixes for morphs/props.
acceptance_criteria: Extend the getRawValue/setRawValue feature-detection pattern to bone rotation control channels in capture()/apply()/apply_full(), or document why bone channels are excluded if there's a reason raw values don't apply there.
close_reason: Extended the getRawValue/setRawValue feature-detection pattern to bone XRotControl/YRotControl/ZRotControl channels in capture()/apply()/apply_full(), matching the existing morphs/props handling; added regression tests.

title: Two-pass viewport capture leaves state unrestored if viewport disappears mid-wait
description: dazpy/_viewport.py:209 - finish_script's 'if (!vp) return null;' guard runs before all of the overlay/selection/tonemapper restore lines. If the active viewport becomes unavailable (closed/changed) during the real wall-clock convergence_wait sleep between prepare_script and finish_script, finish_script returns early and never restores axesOn/floorStyle/showPoseTool/aspectOn/thirdsGuideOn/toolBarMode, the primary selection, or Tonemapper/Environment node visibility -- a state the old atomic single-script capture could never leave the viewport in.
acceptance_criteria: Decide and implement a recovery/restore path for when vp is null in finish_script (e.g. restore against Scene-level state independent of the viewport object, or document the limitation clearly and surface it via a warning/log).
close_reason: finish_script now performs scene-level restoration (selection, Tonemapper/Environment visibility) regardless of vp availability, only skipping viewport-specific properties and the capture itself if vp is gone; added a regression test.

title: Two-pass viewport capture can't restore a bone selection
description: dazpy/_viewport.py:223 - capture()'s primary-selection restore now serializes only the selected node's name across the prepare/finish HTTP round trip and re-resolves it via Scene.findNode(prev.selectionName). The old single-script version held a live object reference and restored it directly. Scene.findNode() resolves top-level scene nodes but not bones or other non-node selectable items (e.g. a bone selected via the Joint Editor), so the original selection is silently lost instead of restored after a capture() call.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a bone before capture() (hide_overlays=True) results in the same bone being selected afterward, not null/no selection. Investigate whether an equivalent bone-lookup API exists to resolve by name.
close_reason: Capture now threads the owning skeleton's name through for bone selections and falls back to skeleton.findBone(name) when Scene.findNode() misses; added a regression test.

title: DPB: token authentication reusing existing SecureRandom
description: Secure the daemon port 18812 endpoints with a token, matching the existing DSS auth model on port 18811, without reimplementing token generation or crypto in Python.
design: DSS remains the sole token generator: reuse AuthenticationService and SecureRandom generateHexToken exactly as done for the existing dazscriptserver_token.txt, writing to a new dazpythonbridge_token.txt under the same daz3d dir with the same chmod-600 enforcement and warning. The Python daemon only ever reads this file at its own startup via an X-DPB-Token header check -- it never generates or rotates a token itself. Single source of truth.
acceptance_criteria: DPB daemon rejects requests without a valid X-DPB-Token; token file is generated by DSS existing SecureRandom-backed code path, not by any Python-side crypto.
close_reason: Dead duplicate from an incomplete migration to the daz-python-bridge repo -- the real, completed copies are daz-python-bridge-sop.1 through .8 (all closed there). daz-python-bridge is now archived; this repo's Package Runner (epic 5sw) is what actually superseded it.

title: DPB: plugin status/management UI and daemon API
description: Non-modal plugin status pane in DSS showing each installed plugin state, resolving, ready, starting, running, failed, or disabled, with start, stop, restart, enable, and disable controls, so users have visibility into background installs and worker health without anything blocking the UI.
design: Daemon exposes GET /plugins, returning state, pid, memory, last-used, and POST /plugins/ID/start, stop, restart, enable, disable. DSS polls via QTimer using async QNetworkAccessManager calls, never a blocking call on the Qt main thread, consistent with the existing AsyncRequestManager polling pattern already used for async DazScript requests. A plugin in resolving or disabled state rejects calls to its exposed_functions with a distinct DazPluginNotReadyError rather than a raw connection failure.
acceptance_criteria: Status pane reflects install progress, running, idle, and failed state, and responds to manual start, stop, restart, enable, disable without freezing the DAZ Studio UI at any point.
close_reason: Dead duplicate from an incomplete migration -- real completed copies are daz-python-bridge-sop.6/.8 (closed).

title: DPB: warm worker process lifecycle and crash policy
description: Each plugin isolated venv needs its own live Python process to actually execute calls, since a venv is not a process. Spawn a persistent warm worker subprocess per plugin lazily on first call, not eagerly, and not spawn-per-call which would pay interpreter startup latency on every invocation.
design: Worker spawned on first /execute call routed to that plugin_id, using that plugin own venv interpreter, communicating over a local pipe or loopback socket. Idle-timeout eviction, for example 10 minutes unused, reclaims memory. Crash policy: one automatic restart on worker crash; if it crashes again, flip to failed state and require manual restart via the status UI -- unlimited silent auto-restart would crash-loop a systematically broken plugin invisibly.
acceptance_criteria: First call to a plugin has a visible but bounded cold start; repeated calls are fast with no re-spawn; an idle plugin worker is reaped after timeout and respawns transparently on next call; a worker that crashes twice in a row ends in failed state, not a restart loop.
close_reason: Dead duplicate from an incomplete migration -- real completed copy is daz-python-bridge-sop.5 (closed).

title: DPB: per-plugin venv isolation and eager dependency resolution
description: Each installed plugin gets its own venv instead of a shared site-packages, so two plugins pinning conflicting dependency versions do not clobber each other. Dependencies are resolved eagerly at install time, right after the zip is committed, not lazily on first call, so a broken requirements.txt surfaces immediately in the plugin status pane instead of on first invocation.
design: uv venv for the plugin dir, then uv pip install -r requirements.txt scoped to that venv. Reuses the Python 3.11 build already downloaded during bootstrap so per-plugin venv creation is sub-second. Disk cost stays low across many plugins because uv global package cache is content-addressable and hardlinks shared packages such as numpy across venvs rather than duplicating them. This replaces the original spec single shared venv with a --target install approach.
acceptance_criteria: Two plugins with conflicting dependency versions install and run without interfering; a plugin with an unresolvable requirements.txt fails at install time, status failed, rather than at first call.
close_reason: Dead duplicate from an incomplete migration -- real completed copy is daz-python-bridge-sop.4 (closed).

title: DPB: /run inline Python execution endpoint + scripting pane
description: Add POST /run to the daemon: executes inline Python in the isolated run_venv, captures print() output as log lines plus a single JSON-serializable return object, mirroring how DazScript inline /execute already works in the other direction. Add a DSS UI pane, Script-IDE style, where users type Python and click Execute.
design: run_venv stays fully isolated -- it must NOT import already-installed plugin packages, keeping it a clean-slate scratch environment like DAZ Studio own Script IDE.
acceptance_criteria: User can type Python in the new pane, execute it, see print() output and the returned value; run_venv has no visibility into plugin venvs.
close_reason: Dead duplicate from an incomplete migration to the daz-python-bridge repo -- the real, completed copies are daz-python-bridge-sop.1 through .8 (all closed there). daz-python-bridge is now archived; this repo's Package Runner (epic 5sw) is what actually superseded it.

title: DPB: daemon bootstrap and JIT venv setup
description: First-run JIT bootstrap for the DPB daemon: download platform uv binary, install Python 3.11 via uv, create the isolated run_venv (used only by the /run inline-scripting endpoint, not by plugins), and launch the FastAPI daemon bound to 127.0.0.1:18812. Everything else in the DPB epic depends on this daemon existing and being launchable/health-checkable from DSS.
design: Layout: AppData/Daz 3D/Studio4/DazPythonBridge/bin/uv, run_venv/, plugins/ID/venv/. Per-plugin venvs are created lazily elsewhere, NOT at bootstrap time -- bootstrap only creates run_venv/. DSS must be able to detect daemon liveness and know if the daemon process died so the plugin status UI can reflect it.
acceptance_criteria: uv and Python 3.11 install triggers on first pane access if missing; run_venv created and isolated from any plugin venv; daemon launches on 18812, bound to loopback only; DSS can detect daemon up/down state.
close_reason: Dead duplicate from an incomplete migration to the daz-python-bridge repo -- the real, completed copies are daz-python-bridge-sop.1 through .8 (all closed there). daz-python-bridge is now archived; this repo's Package Runner (epic 5sw) is what actually superseded it.

title: Daz Python Bridge (DPB): bidirectional Python plugin ecosystem
description: Add a Python daemon (port 18812) that DazScript can call into synchronously, plus a drag-and-drop plugin installer, so DazScript-driven workflows can invoke Python (numpy/ML/HTTP clients) inline and the community can distribute installable Python add-ons for DSS. Complements the existing dazpy client (Python calling INTO DAZ via port 18811) with the reverse direction (DAZ calling INTO Python). Full design worked out gap-by-gap in conversation before implementation; see child issues for the resolved architecture per gap.
design: Two ports: 18811 (existing, DAZ-as-server) unchanged. 18812 (new) is a FastAPI daemon DSS launches. Two venv kinds: an isolated run_venv/ for the inline /run scripting pane (Script-IDE analogue), and one isolated venv per installed plugin under plugins/<id>/venv/ (solves shared-site-packages dependency conflicts). Each plugin gets a lazily-spawned warm worker subprocess (not spawn-per-call) with idle-timeout eviction and a one-shot auto-restart-then-fail-loud crash policy. Zip installs are hardened (miniz, path-traversal/symlink rejection, live-enforced size caps, stage-then-commit atomic install) and dependency-resolved eagerly at install time so failures surface immediately in a non-modal plugin status pane (states: resolving/ready/starting/running/failed/disabled) with start/stop/restart/enable/disable controls. DSS's outbound calls to the daemon use QNetworkAccessManager (async) + QTimer polling, never blocking the Qt main thread. Token auth reuses the existing SecureRandom/AuthenticationService C++ code (DSS generates+owns the token file, daemon only reads it) rather than reimplementing crypto in Python. Reinstall follows the existing script-registry convention (overwrite-by-id), sequenced as stop-worker -> stage-commit -> re-resolve-deps.
acceptance_criteria: All 9 originally-identified spec gaps have a resolved design reflected in child issues; child issues are implementable independently once their listed dependencies are closed.
close_reason: Epic for the duplicate issues closed above -- see daz-python-bridge-sop (closed) for the real history, and daz-script-server-5sw (closed) for what replaced it.

title: Iray Canvas: read/enable existing canvases and return per-canvas output paths
description:
Combined tier 1 + tier 2 of daz-script-server-llr (tier 2 folded in after research confirmed the same API covers both -- see superseded daz-script-server-dwy). GitHub issue #19: expose Iray Canvas enumeration, creation, and per-canvas output paths through dazpy.

Confirmed live-instance API (no C++ server changes needed -- pure DazScript via the existing /execute path, same pattern as the Iray quality-preset code in dazpy/_render.py):

  holder = App.getRenderMgr().getRenderElementObjects()[1]   // DzIrayPropertyHolder

  holder.renderToCanvases: bool                    // master on/off for canvas output
  holder.getNumCanvasDefinitions(): int
  holder.getCanvasDefinition(i): canvas
  holder.findCanvasDefinition(name, createIfMissing): canvas | null
  holder.removeCanvasDefinition(canvas)

  canvas.name: string                              // e.g. 'Canvas1', auto-generated but editable
  canvas.canvasType: int                           // enum -- Beauty=0, Diffuse=1, Specular=2, Glossy=3,
                                                    // Emission=4, LightGroup=5, EnvironmentLighting=6,
                                                    // LPE=7, Irradiance=8, Alpha=9, Shadow=10,
                                                    // AmbientOcclusion=11, Distance=12, Depth=13,
                                                    // MaterialTag=14, MaterialID=15, ObjectID=16,
                                                    // Normal=17, TextureCoordinate=18, BSDFWeight=19,
                                                    // ConvergenceHeatmap=20, PostToon=21, WorldPosition=22
  canvas.canvasTypeToString(int) / canvasTypeFromString(string)
  canvas.index: int

Output file convention (confirmed empirically against a live render): <output_dir>/<basename>_canvases/<basename>-<canvasName>-<canvasTypeString>.exr

renderToCanvases confirmed to actually gate output (folder present/absent both directions, re-tested twice). canvas.processingDisabled does NOT gate per-canvas output -- confirmed it does not skip render even when true; drop it from scope. UI widgets (Render Settings > Advanced > Canvases) do not auto-refresh after scripted property writes -- must call pane.refresh() on MainWindow.getPaneMgr().findPane('DzRenderSettingsPane') after any scripted write to keep the UI in sync; this should be standard practice in the implementation, not just ad hoc during testing.
acceptance_criteria: DazRenderSettings (dazpy/_render.py) gains: list_canvases() (name, type, index), add_canvas(name, canvas_type) using findCanvasDefinition(name, true) + set canvasType, remove_canvas(name), get/set renderToCanvases master toggle (calling pane.refresh() after the write), and a way to retrieve each canvas's resolved output path after a render (derived from the confirmed <basename>-<canvasName>-<canvasTypeString>.exr convention). Unit tests mock DazClient; integration tests scoped with -k against a live DAZ Studio instance per project convention.
close_reason: Canvas enumerate/add/remove/enable/output-path support implemented in dazpy/_render.py; unit tests (10) and live integration tests (5) all pass

title: Add Iray Canvas support to dazpy (normal/depth/material-ID passes)
description: GitHub issue #19 asks for access to Iray's Canvases feature so non-photorealistic/compositing render pipelines built on dazpy can pull normal, depth, material-ID, and other passes without reimplementing geometry projection by hand. Currently there is no dazpy or DazScript-Server call to enumerate, enable, configure, or retrieve output paths for Iray Canvases. Needs: research into the DzIrayRenderer/canvas API surface in DazScript, a server-side handler, and a dazpy-facing method (e.g. on DazRenderSettings) to enable/configure canvases and retrieve their output file paths after a render.
close_reason: Fully implemented and closed via daz-script-server-uae (tier 1+2 combined): canvas enumerate/add/remove/enable + output-path retrieval, covering normal/depth/material-ID and all other canvas types

title: dazpy: add dForce simulation control
description: No DazDforce-equivalent class exists in dazpy for running, baking, or tuning cloth/hair dForce simulation. vangard-daz-mcp's daz_run_dforce_simulation, daz_bake_simulation, and daz_set_dforce_property remain hand-rolled DazScript.
acceptance_criteria: A class or set of methods to trigger a dForce simulation run (with a way to await completion), bake the result onto the mesh, and read/set dForce-specific properties (e.g. on a figure's dForce modifier).
notes: Surfaced during vangard-daz-mcp's dazpy migration audit (2026-07-12). Unblocks 3 tools in wardrobe.py.
close_reason: Added DazDForce modifier class (freeze/unfreeze), DazNode.dforce_modifiers()/find_modifier() type discrimination, and DazScene.run_dforce_simulation()/is_simulating()/clear_dforce_simulation() backed by DzSimulationMgr. Unit + integration tests added.

title: dazpy: add keyframe curve introspection and single-key removal
description: DazProperty.set_key() lets you write a keyframe, but there is no way to read back all keyframes on a curve or remove a single one — only whatever a full clear/overwrite would do. vangard-daz-mcp's daz_get_keyframes, daz_remove_keyframe, and daz_clear_animation remain hand-rolled DazScript.
acceptance_criteria: DazProperty (or DazAnimation) exposes a method to list all keyframes (frame, value) on a property's animation curve, a method to remove a single keyframe at a given frame, and a method to clear the whole curve.
notes: Surfaced during vangard-daz-mcp's dazpy migration audit (2026-07-12). Unblocks 3 tools in animation.py.
close_reason: Implemented get_keys/remove_key/clear_keys on DazProperty

title: dazpy: add clothing fit/unfit support
description: No wrapper exists for DAZ Studio's smart-content fit-to relationship between a figure and clothing/hair items — neither querying what's currently fitted nor fitting/unfitting an item. vangard-daz-mcp's daz_list_fitted_items, daz_fit_clothing, and daz_unfit_item all remain hand-rolled DazScript with no dazpy equivalent.
acceptance_criteria: A method (on DazSkeleton or a new DazFigure-adjacent class) to list items currently fit to a figure, and methods to fit a loaded clothing/hair node to a figure and to unfit/detach it.
notes: Surfaced during vangard-daz-mcp's dazpy migration audit (2026-07-12). Unblocks 3 tools in wardrobe.py.
close_reason: Added fit_to/unfit/fitted_items on DazNode with test coverage

title: dazpy: add node deletion and reparenting
description: No delete()/remove() or set_parent()/reparent() method exists anywhere in the dazpy class surface (DazNode and subclasses). vangard-daz-mcp's daz_delete_node and daz_set_parent tools have no dazpy path and remain on hand-rolled DazScript.
acceptance_criteria: DazNode (or DazScene) exposes a method to remove a node from the scene, and a method to reparent a node to a new parent while optionally preserving its world transform (matching the addNodeChild/removeNodeChild DazScript pattern documented in this repo's SKILL_DAZSCRIPT.md).
notes: Surfaced during vangard-daz-mcp's dazpy migration audit (2026-07-12). Unblocks 2 tools in transform.py.
close_reason: Added DazNode.delete() and DazNode.reparent(), verified against a live DAZ Studio instance

title: dazpy: add node-creation factory for cameras and lights
description: dazpy wraps existing scene nodes (DazCamera, DazLight, etc.) but has no factory method to create new ones — the whole class surface assumes the node already exists in the scene. This blocks vangard-daz-mcp's daz_create_camera, daz_create_light, daz_set_active_camera (needs a camera to exist before it can be made active), and two cinematic rig-builders (daz_setup_shot_coverage, daz_create_camera_rig) from ever moving off hand-rolled DazScript onto dazpy.
acceptance_criteria: DazScene (or a new factory) exposes a method to create a new DzBasicCamera/DzSpotLight/DzPointLight/DzDistantLight and add it to the scene, returning a wrapper (DazCamera/DazLight) usable with the rest of the existing API (set_position, aim_at, set_color, etc.). Covers at minimum: basic camera, spot/point/distant light.
notes: Surfaced during vangard-daz-mcp's dazpy migration audit (2026-07-12). Unblocks 5 tools across camera_light.py and cinematic.py.
close_reason: Added DazScene.create_camera() and DazScene.create_light() factory methods, unblocking 5 vangard-daz-mcp tools

title: Publish dazpy to PyPI on tagged releases
description:
The build-dazpy.yml workflow builds a wheel and uploads it as a CI artifact, but there is no step that publishes it to PyPI. On tagged releases (v*.*.*) we should publish to PyPI using OIDC trusted publishing (pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish), which avoids needing a stored API token.

Changes needed:
1. build-dazpy.yml: build both wheel + sdist (python -m build without --wheel flag), rename artifact from dazpy-wheel to dazpy-dist
2. release-tagged.yml: add publish-pypi job (needs build-dazpy), add id-token: write permission, update artifact reference from dazpy-wheel to dazpy-dist
3. release-nightly.yml: update dazpy-wheel artifact reference to dazpy-dist
4. Update .github/workflows/*.md docs to reflect the new publish step and OIDC requirement
close_reason: Implemented: build-dazpy now builds wheel+sdist, release-tagged.yml has publish-pypi job using OIDC, artifact renamed to dazpy-dist everywhere, docs updated

title: Upgrade Xcode on self-hosted macOS Intel runner (ORION) for SDK6 builds
description: The self-hosted Intel Mac runner 'ORION' used for macOS Intel CI builds (build-macos.yml, runs-on: [self-hosted, macOS, X64]) only has Xcode 14.1 / AppleClang 14 (macOS 13.1 SDK) via Command Line Tools. Qt 6.10.3 (used for DAZ Studio 6 SDK builds) requires a newer libc++/Clang to compile qhash.h's QKeyValueIterator/QKeyValueRange constructs cleanly. The macOS Intel DS6 leg of test-build.yml fails to compile with errors like 'no template named QKeyValueIterator' even after the qt4_patches include-overlay scoping fix (daz-script-server-017) was applied and confirmed working on the GitHub-hosted macos-14-arm64 runner. Needs Xcode 15+ installed and selected via xcode-select on ORION, then re-verify via workflow_dispatch test-build.yml with platform=macos-intel sdk-version=6.
acceptance_criteria: macOS Intel DS6 leg of test-build.yml passes after Xcode upgrade on ORION
close_reason: Superseded: retargeted macOS Intel build (build-macos.yml) to GitHub-hosted macos-13 runner instead of self-hosted ORION, with explicit Xcode 15.2 selection for the SDK6 leg. Avoids needing a macOS/Xcode upgrade on ORION (stuck at Monterey 12.7.5, can't host Xcode 15+).

title: Fix: changing server port doesn't stop the old listener thread
description: Discovered during DS6 testing: changing the port in the pane's Settings UI (e.g. 18811 -> 18812) without restarting DAZ Studio leaves the OLD listener thread/httplib::Server bound and serving requests in addition to the new one - both ports end up live simultaneously against the same DzScriptServerPane instance, served by a single process. This is a real bug in the start/stop/apply-settings logic (likely onStartClicked()/applySettings() needs to fully stop the previous ServerListenThread/httplib::Server before starting a new one on the new port), not just a testing artifact - confirmed by curl'ing both ports and getting live responses from both after a port change with no restart.
close_reason: Fixed: stopServer() was deleting the httplib::Server object before joining the listener thread, a use-after-free race; the freed memory could be reused by the next startServer() call, leaving both old and new listeners apparently live. Reordered to join/terminate the thread before deleting the Server object.

title: Run new CI workflows end-to-end and fix issues found

title: Main orchestrator script (main.py)
description:
Build the main.py entry point that wires together the viewport snapshot, file watcher, and ComfyUI submission into a single runnable workflow.

## Why
The individual components (viewport capture, file watcher, ComfyUI client) are usable independently, but the orchestrator is what makes this a working example. It should be runnable with a single command and show clear progress output.

## What needs to be done
- main.py CLI with argparse:
  - --config path to config file (optional, falls back to defaults)
  - --output path for the final enhanced image
  - --denoise override denoise strength
  - --no-watch skip file watcher, expect the snapshot path directly (--snapshot-path)
  - --dry-run print what would happen without executing
- Execution flow:
  1. Load config (merge CLI args)
  2. Connect dazpy client (DazClient), verify server health
  3. Connect ComfyUI client, verify /system_stats
  4. Set up file watcher on watch_dir
  5. Call DazViewport.capture(watch_dir/snapshot.png, width, height)
  6. Wait for watcher to return the file path
  7. Upload image to ComfyUI (client.upload_image)
  8. Build workflow from template (workflow_builder.build)
  9. Submit workflow (client.queue_prompt)
  10. Wait for result (client.wait_for_result) with progress dots
  11. Download and save output to --output path
  12. Print summary: input path, output path, duration
- Error handling: clear messages for server not running, file not found, timeout

## Design decisions
- Use --no-watch mode for development/testing when you already have a source image
- Always print the output path at the end so it can be piped or opened programmatically

## Acceptance criteria
- python main.py runs end-to-end with both servers running
- --dry-run prints plan without executing
- Error messages are human-readable (not stack traces) for the common failure cases
close_reason: Implemented as part of examples/comfyui_enhance/ pipeline

title: img2img ComfyUI workflow template (workflow.json)
description:
Create a ComfyUI workflow JSON template tuned for photorealistic enhancement of DAZ Studio viewport captures.

## Why
ComfyUI workflows are parameterized JSON graphs. The template must be designed for img2img enhancement — not text-to-image generation — with settings biased toward sharpness, detail retention, and photorealism rather than creative deviation.

## What needs to be done
- Create workflow.json as a standard ComfyUI API-format (prompt dict, not UI format)
- Nodes to include:
  1. CheckpointLoaderSimple — loads a photorealistic SDXL or SD1.5 checkpoint
  2. LoadImage — references the uploaded input image
  3. VAEEncode — encode input image to latent
  4. CLIPTextEncode (positive) — fixed prompt: 'photorealistic, sharp focus, high detail, 8k, professional photography, clean lighting'
  5. CLIPTextEncode (negative) — '(blurry, low quality, noise, artifact, watermark:1.4), painterly, cartoon, drawing'
  6. KSampler — denoise=0.45, steps=20, cfg=7.0, sampler=dpmpp_2m, scheduler=karras
  7. VAEDecode — decode back to pixel space
  8. SaveImage — writes to ComfyUI output folder
- Parameterize via Python string substitution for: checkpoint_name, denoise_strength, steps, positive_prompt override
- workflow_builder.py — Python module that loads the template and fills in parameters, returning a dict ready for queue_prompt()

## Design decisions
- denoise=0.45 as default: strong enough to improve quality, low enough to preserve scene composition and character positions
- Use DPM++ 2M Karras for quality/speed balance
- Keep positive prompt minimal and generic so it works across scene types without fighting the source content

## Acceptance criteria
- workflow_builder.build(image_ref, config) returns a valid ComfyUI prompt dict
- Can be loaded and submitted to a real ComfyUI instance without modification errors
close_reason: Implemented as part of examples/comfyui_enhance/ pipeline

title: File watcher module (file_watcher.py)
description:
Build a file watcher that monitors a directory for a new image file and triggers a callback when the file is fully written.

## Why
DAZ Studio's captureToFile() is fire-and-forget from the script side — it writes to disk but the dazpy client doesn't know the exact moment the file is ready. A file watcher decouples the capture trigger from the ComfyUI submission and handles the write-completion race condition reliably.

## What needs to be done
- FileWatcher class using the watchdog library:
  - watch(directory: str, callback: Callable[[str], None], pattern: str = '*.png', timeout: float = 30.0) -> str
  - Blocks until a matching file appears in the directory and is fully written
  - Write-completion detection: poll file size until it stops growing (100ms interval, 3 stable readings)
  - Returns the full path of the detected file
  - Raises TimeoutError if timeout elapses with no file
- Also support async-style: watch_async() that starts a background thread and calls callback when ready
- cleanup: remove the handler after first match (one-shot mode by default)

## Design decisions
- watchdog Observer is heavier than polling but handles network drives and non-inotify systems correctly on Windows
- One-shot mode is correct for this pipeline (one capture → one submission)
- Write-completion by size stability is more reliable than a fixed sleep

## Acceptance criteria
- Unit test: mock watchdog events, assert callback fires with correct path
- Integration test: write a file to a temp dir, assert watch() returns the path

title: ComfyUI HTTP API client module
description:
Build a self-contained ComfyUI client module (comfyui_client.py) that handles all HTTP communication with a local ComfyUI instance.

## Why
ComfyUI exposes a REST+WebSocket API that is not officially documented but is well understood from community usage. Encapsulating it in a client class keeps the orchestrator clean and makes the client independently testable.

## What needs to be done
- ComfyUIClient class with:
  - __init__(base_url='http://127.0.0.1:8188', client_id=None)
  - upload_image(path: str) -> str — POST /upload/image, returns 'subfolder/filename'
  - queue_prompt(workflow: dict) -> str — POST /prompt, returns prompt_id
  - get_history(prompt_id: str) -> dict — GET /history/{prompt_id}
  - wait_for_result(prompt_id: str, timeout: float = 120.0) -> dict — polls get_history until outputs appear
  - download_image(filename: str, subfolder: str = '', folder_type: str = 'output') -> bytes — GET /view
  - save_result(prompt_id: str, output_path: str, timeout: float = 120.0) -> str — combines wait + download + save
  - get_system_stats() -> dict — GET /system_stats (for health check)
- All methods raise ComfyUIError (custom exception) on non-2xx responses
- Polling in wait_for_result uses exponential backoff (0.5s → 2s max)

## Design decisions
- Use requests library not httpx (simpler, no async needed for this workflow)
- client_id is a UUID generated once per instance, used in prompt submissions
- No WebSocket — polling is sufficient for batch workflows

## Acceptance criteria
- Unit tests cover upload, queue, wait, download with mocked requests
- ComfyUIError raised correctly on HTTP errors
- save_result() produces a file on disk given a valid ComfyUI instance

title: Move UsdExportServer to worker thread to unblock status reads during export
description:

title: Add POST /render/batch endpoint for variant rendering
description:
VN production requires rendering many variants of the same scene (expressions, poses) — often 10-30 per character setup. Submitting each individually requires many round trips and makes orchestration harder.

Implement POST /render/batch that accepts a base config plus a list of variants, enqueues each variant as an independent async render request, and returns all request_ids in one response.

Request schema:
  base: {camera, width, height, engine, figure} — shared settings
  variants: [{output_path, morphs, figures, ...overrides}] — per-render settings

Each variant is an independent AsyncRequest with isRender=true. Returns:
  {batch_id: 'bat-...', request_ids: [...], total: N}

Key design point: variants render sequentially (DAZ cannot render two scenes simultaneously), but the HTTP client can interleave other requests between polls. Document both usage patterns:
  Pattern A: submit full batch upfront, poll all request_ids
  Pattern B: submit one at a time, use setup between renders for complex scene changes

Atomicity: if variant N fails, variants N+1..M still render. Per-variant errors in results.
notes: Implemented. POST /render/batch accepts {base, variants:[]}. Base provides optional defaults (camera, width, height, engine, figure/figures, reset_morphs). Each variant requires output_path; merges with base for remaining fields. Figure merge: variant figures/figure wins; variant morphs+single base figure merges morphs (variant overrides). All variants validated and pre-flighted before any are enqueued (fail-fast). Enqueue failures mid-batch return 503 with partial count. Response: {batch_id:'bat-...', request_ids:[...], total:N}. Each rnd-id compatible with existing /requests/:id/status, /requests/:id/result, and GET /render/:id/progress endpoints. Max 100 variants per batch.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add GET /render/:id/progress SSE endpoint
notes: Implemented. New RenderProgressBroker class (plain C++, no QObject) manages per-render SSE subscriber queues. Route: GET /render/:id/progress (auth-gated, SSE with keepalives). Events emitted: 'progress' (percent:0) when render starts executing, 'complete' (output_path, file_size_bytes, duration_ms) or 'error' on finish. Late-joining clients receive stored terminal event immediately. DAZ SDK has no renderProgress(int) signal — DzRenderer only exposes aboutToRender/renderFinished — so no real per-percent progress is possible. Render identity detected by 'rnd-' id prefix.

title: Wire SceneEventBroker into server lifecycle
description:
Integrate broker into DzScriptServerPane start/stop.

Changes to DzScriptServerPane.h:
- Add: SceneEventBroker* m_pEventBroker;

Changes to DzScriptServerPane.cpp:

onStartClicked() / server start path:
- Instantiate m_pEventBroker = new SceneEventBroker(this)
- Call m_pEventBroker->start() -- connects to DzScene signals
- Register GET /scene/events route, passing m_pEventBroker to handler lambda

onStopClicked() / server stop path:
- Call m_pEventBroker->stop() -- disconnects signals, closes all subscriber queues (so SSE handlers exit cleanly)
- delete m_pEventBroker; m_pEventBroker = nullptr;

Server stop must drain SSE handlers before returning. stop() should call queue->close() on all registered queues and then briefly wait (or just let handler threads exit naturally -- httplib will wait for handlers on server stop).

title: SSE endpoint GET /scene/events
description:
Add SSE handler in DzScriptServerPane.cpp (alongside existing handlers).

Route: GET /scene/events

Query params:
- filter= comma-separated list of categories: node,skeleton,light,camera,selection,scene,time,render
  Default (omitted): all categories enabled

Handler logic:
1. Check auth (reuse existing token validation)
2. Check IP whitelist (reuse existing check)
3. Parse ?filter= into bitmask
4. Set response headers: Content-Type: text/event-stream, Cache-Control: no-cache, Connection: keep-alive
5. Create SubscriberQueue, register with m_pEventBroker
6. Loop:
   a. pop(15000) -- 15s timeout
   b. If empty (timeout): write ':keepalive\n\n', flush -- client detects disconnect on failed flush
   c. If event: write 'data: <json>\n\n', flush
   d. If flush fails (client gone): break
7. Unregister SubscriberQueue from broker, delete queue

Note: httplib keeps the handler alive for the duration -- this is a long-running handler, same pattern as the existing long-poll result handler.
close_reason: SSE handler added to setupRoutes() in DzScriptServerPane.cpp: auth check, filter parsing, SubscriberQueue lifecycle, chunked content provider loop with keepalive

title: Debounce timers for high-frequency signals
description:
Add debounce logic inside SceneEventBroker for signals that fire at high frequency.

Signals needing debounce:
1. timeChanging() -- fires every frame during playback (~30-60fps)
   Strategy: on timeChanging, start/restart a 150ms QTimer (single-shot)
   On timer fire: emit one time.changed event with current scene time
   On timeChanged() (manual scrub): emit immediately, cancel timer

2. nodeSelectionListChanged() -- can burst during multi-select
   Strategy: 50ms debounce, coalesce into single selection.list_changed

Implementation:
- QTimer* m_pTimeDebounce (150ms, single-shot)
- QTimer* m_pSelectionDebounce (50ms, single-shot)
- Both owned by SceneEventBroker (main thread), so no thread-safety issues
- Store pending time value so debounced slot has current value on fire
close_reason: Implemented in SceneEventBroker.cpp: 150ms debounce for timeChanging, 50ms for nodeSelectionListChanged

title: JSON event serialization for all event types
description:
Implement serializeEvent() in SceneEventBroker for each signal category.

Output format per event:
  {"type":"node.added","ts":1716307200123,"data":{...}}

Event types and their data payloads:
- scene.loading, scene.loaded, scene.saving, scene.saved(filename), scene.clear_starting, scene.cleared
- node.added(node_id, node_name, node_type), node.removed(node_id, node_name), node.list_changed
- skeleton.added(node_id, node_name), skeleton.removed(node_id, node_name)
- light.added(node_id, node_name, node_type), light.removed(node_id, node_name)
- camera.added(node_id, node_name), camera.removed(node_id, node_name)
- selection.list_changed, selection.primary_changed(node_id, node_name) -- empty data{} if null
- time.changed(time_value, fps), playback.started, playback.finished
- render.started, render.finished

Use existing JsonBuilder for safe serialization. Extract node_id via node->getElementID() or similar DAZ SDK call -- verify exact method name against SDK headers.
close_reason: Implemented in SceneEventBroker.cpp: makeEvent(), nodeInfoJson(), per-slot JsonBuilder calls for all event types

title: SceneEventBroker and SubscriberQueue classes
description:
Create include/SceneEventBroker.h and src/SceneEventBroker.cpp.

SceneEventBroker (QObject, main thread):
- Connects to dzApp->getScene() signals via Qt::DirectConnection on start()
- Disconnects all signals on stop()
- Maintains QMutex-protected list of SubscriberQueue*
- registerSubscriber(queue, filter_mask) and unregisterSubscriber(queue)
- Internal: serializeEvent(type, data) -> QString JSON

SubscriberQueue (one per SSE client):
- QMutex + QWaitCondition + std::deque<QString>
- push(const QString& event) -- called from main thread
- pop(int timeout_ms) -> QString -- called from HTTP thread, blocks
- close() -- signals the queue is done (server stopping)

Filter mask: bitmask of event categories (node, selection, scene, time, render, light, camera, skeleton).

title: SSE streams end by aborting the connection instead of sink.done()
description: Found while fixing alaz. The /render/{id}/progress chunked provider (src/DzScriptServerPane.cpp, set_chunked_content_provider ~line 1714, and likely the /events one ~1629) returns false once the queue closes. Fix: call sink.done() and return true after the terminal event / on close.

title: math3.Quat vs Studio DzQuat: components are conjugates
description: Live-verified 2026-11-19 (5d6f.20): for a camera with rotation channels (x,y,z), DzNode.getWSRot() returns quaternion components that are the conjugate (x,y,z negated) of math3.Quat.from_euler(x,y,z,'ZYX'). (Its multVec(-Z) still matches math3's matrix, so DzQuat.multVec uses the opposite convention.) math3's module docstring suggests Quat.from_dict(bone.local_rotation) / DazNode.rotation directly, which yields the inverse rotation. Also: camera Euler channels compose as math3 order 'ZYX' while Studio reports rotation order 'XYZ', and Quat.from_euler docs claim to match DazBone.rotation_order. shot_library.euler_from_quaternion conjugates explicitly. Audit math3 docs/consumers (bones too) and either document or add a from_dz/to_dz pair.
acceptance_criteria: math3 documents the DzQuat convention and offers a correct conversion; bone usage verified live
close_reason: Added Quat.from_dz/to_dz and from_dz_euler/to_dz_euler (dazpy + daz-ts). Live-verified on DS4 Genesis 9 bones + camera: DzQuat = conjugate of math3 quat (getLocalRot/getWSRot/getOrientation); math3 order = reversed Studio rotation order; local = O*from_euler*O^-1 with O=from_dz(getOrientation()). Round-trip through set_local_rotation/local_rotation matches; docs corrected.
