title: daz-mcp-server: migrate embedded DazScripts onto dazpy primitives
description: daz-mcp-server carries ~106 embedded DazScripts (src/vangard_daz_mcp/_registry.py, ~8,000 lines) registered with the server at startup. About 85 tool call sites go through them via _execute_by_id instead of dazpy. Whole tool modules never touch dazpy: cinematic (22 tools), render (17), wardrobe (16), camera_light (15), content, hair, workflow. Several capabilities exist twice and drift apart: camera framing/orbit (vangard-frame-camera-to-node vs cinematics.apply_frame_subject), lighting presets vs lighting.py, apply pose, clothing fitting, dForce, materials. ASSESSMENT.md says dazpy should own the typed domain primitives and the MCP server should translate intent into plans. 5d6f.20 covers only the cinematic slice. This issue covers the rest: for each embedded script, either replace the tool body with existing dazpy calls, add the missing primitive to dazpy first, or document why it must stay MCP-side (e.g. Windows UI automation for wearable save).
acceptance_criteria: Inventory of every _registry.py script, classified as replace / add-to-dazpy / keep-with-reason; duplicated capabilities route through dazpy; the registry shrinks accordingly with MCP tests green.
notes:
2026-11-24 inventory (daz-mcp-server master 6539a5b, dazpy 2.16.0): about 100 of 165 tools still send DazScript. Per-module issues in daz-mcp-server beads: transform bzh, scene 14w, utility ksl, figure dnj, cinematic ord, camera_light qrd, render k6j, material et7, morph 96d (in progress), animation scz, wardrobe 1kd; content/hair decision z2h; unused registered scripts b7q. Gaps that need new dazpy API (file here when picked up): dForce dynamic surfaces / influence weights / surface properties, transfer utility, ERC, content browser / asset save (overlaps 5d6f.21), strand hair, node lookup by elementID/path (daz-mcp-server nde). By-design exceptions: daz_execute, daz_execute_file_async, daz_validate_script.

2026-11-24 morph slice done: dazpy primitives DazNode.set_numeric_candidates, DazSkeleton.set_bone_axes/bone_names, DazScene.viewport_camera (d7d7d13) plus DazBone inherited-method locator fix (adb82c9), branch feat/morph-tool-primitives-5d6f29. MCP morph tools migrated on daz-mcp-server branch feat/morph-tools-dazpy-96d (a065357; 96d/3oq/7w8/w88 closed), vangard-set-emotion removed. Next: dazpy 2.17 release + MCP floor bump (daz-mcp-server-88c). Still open: daz_set_morph/list/search_morphs need nde-style property search; cinematic emotion script bug onf.
close_reason: Done 2026-11-25. Registry 107 -> 5 scripts. All other tools now run on dazpy primitives (dazpy branch feat/morph-tool-primitives-5d6f29 up to 0a50ffe; MCP branch feat/morph-tools-dazpy-96d up to b19c302); no tool sends inline DazScript. Kept on purpose, each with a code comment: wearable preset save and strand-hair creation (Studio dialogs; strand hair gets opt-in UIA auto_confirm), ERC freeze (no dazpy ERC editing API), find-actions (DzActionMgr), OBJ import (silent unit-scale DzObjImporter). daz_execute/execute_file/validate_script run your own script by design. Not pushed; the dazpy 2.17 release and MCP floor bump are tracked in daz-mcp-server-88c.

title: Stream animation frame progress over /render/{id}/progress SSE on Studio 6
description: 5d6f.12 added frame N of M to job status on both SDKs (server-owned frame report read by polling workers on Studio 6). The SSE stream GET /render/{id}/progress still gets frame events only on Studio 4, because RenderProgressBroker::notifyProgress is fed by the [DAZPY_FRAME] print marker, and Studio 6 shims print() into an array. Fix: have the SSE handler (HTTP thread) poll AsyncRequestManager for frame progress changes on Studio 6, or have status ingestion push into the broker.
notes: Implemented in cf8a19c (fix/assessment-p1): SSE handler polls frameProgress() on DS6, broker dedupes + replays latest frame. Builds DS4+DS6, 801 unit tests + parity pass. PENDING: live check - install DS6 build, run python tests/smoke_live.py --stages render --engines viewport and confirm sse_frames non-empty, then close.
close_reason: Live-verified on DS6 6.26 (2.11.0 build w/ cf8a19c): 24-frame viewport animation streamed frames [3,7,11,14,18,22]/24 strictly increasing then complete; late subscriber got latest frame replayed. Full smoke matrix 27 pass / 0 fail / 2 skip (filament unregistered, mcp).

title: daz-bridge-usd: return ErrorResponse envelope from /export/usd routes
description: The daz-bridge-usd companion plugin's /export/usd handlers return errors as {"error":"..."} (UsdExportServer::errorJson) instead of the ErrorResponse envelope {success:false,error_code,error,retryable}. openapi.yaml documents this as PluginError. Switching the plugin to ErrorResponse (e.g. MISSING_FIELD, INVALID_JSON, REQUEST_NOT_FOUND) would let clients handle every route the same way; afterwards, drop PluginError from the spec. Lives in the daz-bridge-usd repo.
close_reason: Won't fix: USD export is shelved. 17f74b2 already removed /export/usd and PluginError from openapi.yaml and the dazpy USD calls. A plugin-side envelope change (c77aafc in daz-bridge-usd) was made and then dropped unpushed. If USD export returns, its routes should use ErrorResponse from the start.

title: Artifact image thumbnails/previews for GET /artifacts
description: Follow-up to 5d6f.7 (ASSESSMENT #6 'thumbnail/preview generation for images'). Add e.g. GET /artifacts/{id}/{artifact_id}?thumbnail=<px> returning a scaled PNG/JPEG for image artifacts. Deferred from 5d6f.7 because image decoding needs QImage (QtGui) and its format plugins: safety off the main thread on a raw httplib std::thread is unverified for Qt 4.8 (DS4), and EXR/HDR need extra handling. Options: decode on the main thread via a queued call with a busy fallback, or cache a thumbnail at declaration time.

title: build.sh build reuses INSTALL_TO_DAZ=ON from a previous install
description: After './build.sh install', CMakeCache keeps INSTALL_TO_DAZ=ON. A later './build.sh build' does not reconfigure, so the linker writes straight into the DAZ plugins folder and fails with LNK1104 while DAZ Studio is running. Fix: pass -DINSTALL_TO_DAZ=OFF for the build command and reconfigure when the cache has it ON. Workaround: cmake -B build[-sdk6] -DINSTALL_TO_DAZ=OFF.

title: daz-ts Phase 1 cleanup: minor findings from final whole-branch review
description:
Deferred Minor findings from the daz-ts Phase 1 final whole-branch review (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-06-daz-ts-phase1.md), not blocking merge but worth addressing early in Phase 2 (daz-script-server-56nz) before more code builds on the same patterns:

- client.ts: unnecessary dynamic import('./batch.js') in executeBatchAsync (no real circular-import risk since batch.ts's DazClient import is type-only; a static import is simpler)
- client.ts: getRequestStatus/getRequestResult call resp.json() directly without mapping 401/403 to AuthenticationError first (unlike listRequests/status/health/metrics/exportUsdSubmit), so an expired token mid-poll surfaces a raw JSON-parse SyntaxError instead of AuthenticationError. Inherited from dazpy's same wart but worth fixing on the port.
- client.ts raiseForError: non-JSON error bodies (e.g. a 502 from an intermediary, or a 413 with an HTML body) throw a raw JSON-parse SyntaxError instead of a DazError. Wrap in try/catch, fall back to a generic DazError.
- client.ts fetchWithTimeout: timeoutMs only bounds time-to-headers (cleared in .finally() once fetch() resolves); the subsequent response-body read (resp.json()) is unbounded, unlike Python requests' timeout which covers the read too.
- client.ts streamRenderProgress/streamSceneEvents: streamTimeoutMs only bounds time-to-first-byte (same clearTimeout-in-finally issue), which is misleading for a method whose whole point is a long-lived stream; these two also bypass fetchWithTimeout (no ConnectionError mapping) and swallow auth failures into null. Consider accepting an external AbortSignal instead.
- client.ts parseSseStream: only matches \n\n (LF) as the block delimiter, not CRLF. No live impact (verified the C++ server emits \n\n in DzScriptServerPane.cpp/RenderProgressBroker.cpp) but is an undocumented coupling to server framing.
- batch.ts: Batch.add() (unlike addOperation()) bypasses the maxOperations limit entirely, since only addOperation increments/checks the counter meaningfully relative to the cap. Matches dazpy but undermines the cap's stated purpose.
- index.ts: doesn't re-export DEFAULT_MAX_OPERATIONS/DEFAULT_MAX_SCRIPT_LENGTH from batch.ts, so a consumer configuring BatchOptions can't reference the shipped defaults.
- tsconfig.json: include only covers src/, so npm run build never type-checks test/; Vitest transpiles tests without type-checking them, so a type error in a test would ship silently. Add a typecheck script/tsconfig covering both, run in CI.
- exceptions.ts: MaterialError's requestId doc comment is copy-pasted from RenderError ('The server-assigned render request ID') and is wrong for MaterialError.
- Multiple test files (batch/injection/polling vs execute/async/render) each define their own local jsonResponse(...) helper with two incompatible signatures ((body) vs (status, body)). Extract to a shared test/helpers.ts.
- math3.ts: Vec3.fromList doesn't validate array length; with noUncheckedIndexedAccess off, Vec3.fromList([1,2]) silently produces a Vec3 with z: undefined typed as number.
acceptance_criteria: Each bullet above is either fixed or explicitly re-triaged (accepted as intentional/low-value) with a one-line rationale recorded on this issue before closing.
close_reason: All 12 bullets fixed on feature/daz-ts-phase1 (c426c4f, 07f02ac, d5a21d8): (1) static batch import; (2) getRequestStatus/Result map 401/403 via raiseForError; (3) non-JSON error bodies -> DazError; (4) fetchWithTimeout buffers body inside the timer (long-poll gets waitTimeout+10s, artifact downloads stream); (5) stream methods take {timeoutMs, signal}: timeout caps whole stream lifetime, signal cancels, throw ConnectionError/AuthenticationError instead of null, body cancelled on early exit, listener/timer cleaned up (live-checked: socket closes 18ms after break); (6) CRLF/CR parsing incl. split CRLF and trailing CR at EOF; (7) Batch.add counts toward maxOperations; (8) DEFAULT_MAX_* exported; (9) tsconfig.typecheck.json + npm typecheck + CI step (found/fixed 11 latent test type errors); (10) MaterialError doc; (11) shared test/helpers.ts jsonResponse(body, status, headers); (12) Vec3.fromList length check. BREAKING: stream methods' 2nd param is now an options object. 580 unit tests; integration suite not run live.

title: dazpy math3.Quat.from_euler has a sign bug in the ZYX rotation-order branch
description: _euler_to_quat() in dazpy/math3.py computes the wrong w (scalar) component for rotation order 'ZYX': it returns cx*cy*cz - sx*sy*sz, but hand-deriving the composition qz.multiply(qy).multiply(qx) via the Hamilton product formula (the same formula implemented in Quat.multiply) gives cx*cy*cz + sx*sy*sz. Verified numerically: for angles x=10, y=20, z=15 degrees, Quat.from_euler(10,20,15,'ZYX').w comes out as 0.9706917153571218 vs the correct 0.9746425959363222 from composing already-verified primitives; x/y/z components match in both. quatToEuler's ZYX branch is correct (round-trips correctly when fed the correct quaternion), so the bug is isolated to _euler_to_quat's ZYX branch's w sign. All other 5 rotation orders (XYZ, XZY, YXZ, YZX, ZXY) were spot-checked and are correct. Discovered while porting math3.py to daz-ts (TypeScript SDK); daz-ts's own port fixes the sign since it has no reason to stay bug-compatible, but dazpy itself still ships the bug and should be fixed with a regression test added to test_dazpy.py's TestQuat class for ZYX round-trip.
acceptance_criteria: _euler_to_quat's ZYX branch returns w = cx*cy*cz + sx*sy*sz; a new test in TestQuat asserts Quat.from_euler(x,y,z,'ZYX').to_euler('ZYX') round-trips for at least 2-3 non-gimbal-lock angle sets, matching the existing XYZ round-trip test's style.
close_reason: Fix was already present in math3.py; added regression tests (extra ZYX angle sets + Hamilton-product cross-check) to tests/test_dazpy.py

title: scene.find_skeleton() intermittently fails to resolve a valid skeleton name under restore() load
description:
Observed twice while live-validating daz-script-server-jz0e's fix (Genesis 9
"Jason Cross" scene, DazSceneState.apply() driving all 11 skeletons through
pose-restore + verify + follow-target-fix in one call -- ~20-30+ HTTP
round trips in quick succession):

DazSceneState.apply()'s per-skeleton loop reported "Skeleton not found:
Genesis9Eyelashes" (once) and, on a later run, both "Genesis9Eyelashes" and
"Genesis9Tear" (same run). In both cases, calling scene.find_skeleton() for
the exact same name immediately afterward, standalone, succeeded -- so the
skeleton was never actually missing; the lookup transiently failed only
under the load of the surrounding restore() call.

Impact so far: benign. Both affected items had no pose data to restore in
either occurrence (their own capture() was empty), so no visible scene
corruption resulted -- but this is separate flakiness from
daz-script-server-jz0e's actual bug (which is confirmed fixed: fit-to
relationships held correctly across all these same runs, including the
ones with this find_skeleton flakiness). Worth investigating if it starts
affecting a skeleton that *does* have real pose data to restore -- that
would show up as an incorrectly-reported-error (or worse, a silently
unrestored pose) for a skeleton that's actually fine.

Possibly related to DzScriptServerPane::isMainThreadBusy()'s documented
lazy-content-streaming tail (see mainThreadBusyMessage()'s new
DzBackgroundProgress/DzProgress distinction, added same session) -- but
find_skeleton() itself has no retry_on_busy option and this failure mode
doesn't surface as a 503 at all (Scene.getSkeletonList() just returns an
incomplete list momentarily), so it isn't caught by the existing busy
detection/retry machinery either way.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
- Root cause understood (scene-graph iteration racing with concurrent
  main-thread mutation from other skeletons' apply_full() calls in the
  same burst, most likely) or reproduced in isolation.
- find_skeleton() (or DazSceneState.apply()'s use of it) made reliable
  under this load pattern -- retry-with-backoff on a momentary miss, or a
  fix to whatever race causes Scene.getSkeletonList() to be incomplete.
design: Root cause: Scene.getSkeletonList() races against DAZ Studio's own deferred/background scene-graph work (see mainThreadBusyMessage()'s documented lazy-content-streaming tail and the related dpi-mxq partial-main-thread-execution-under-contention issue) -- neither is observable or controllable from the DazScript/HTTP side, and the only externally visible symptom is a momentary false miss on an item that is confirmed present a moment later. True root-cause fix would require DAZ Studio SDK-side instrumentation we don't have; per this issue's own acceptance criteria, resolved via retry-with-backoff instead.
notes: Implemented in dazpy/_scene.py DazScene.find_skeleton(): up to 3 getSkeletonList() lookups (configurable via retry_attempts/retry_delay), short linear backoff (0.15s * attempt) between misses, before falling through to the existing hint-building/NodeNotFoundError path. find_skeleton_by_label() was left untouched -- same underlying race is plausible there but no failure was observed/reported against it; can extend later if it recurs. Not root-caused in the sense of a live Studio repro (would require the same restore() burst load that has previously frozen Studio -- avoided per prior session guidance on not running the full live integration suite); the fix targets the class of transient miss regardless of exact internal DAZ Studio mechanism.
close_reason: Added retry-with-backoff to DazScene.find_skeleton() for the transient Scene.getSkeletonList() miss described in the bug; likely tied to DAZ Studio's own deferred/background scene-graph work (same family as dpi-mxq), which isn't independently observable from the DazScript/HTTP side. Covered by new unit tests; full test suite green.

title: Expose camera aperture / bokeh controls (DOF blur intensity)
description: GitHub issue #25 (split from #20, last remaining item). DzCamera exposed depth_of_field/focal_length/focal_distance but nothing controlling DOF blur intensity or bokeh shape.
close_reason: Added DazCamera.f_stop, .aperture_blades, .aperture_blade_rotation (dazpy/_camera.py). Property labels confirmed against a live DAZ Studio instance: 'F/Stop' (name 'Aperature'), 'Aperture Blades', 'Aperture Blade Rotation' -- all present on DzBasicCamera/DzCamera and writable. Verified read/write round-trip live, then cleaned up the test camera. Unit tests added (6 new), full suite (671 tests) passes.

title: Iray intra-frame percent via log parsing (conditional on spike)
description: Only if the spike issue confirms Iray posts parseable progress text through onMessagePosted: add a small regex-based RenderLogProgressParser invoked from onMessagePosted while m_currentRenderId is set. Throttle emission (>=1% change or >=500ms) via lastPercent/lastEmitMs tracked per request in RenderProgressBroker's RequestWatch. Feed into notifyProgress(), combined with frame info for animation renders.
close_reason: Closed

title: dazpy.materials: IrayMaterial/TextureMap/SurfaceProperty submodule (GH #31 item 2c)
description: GitHub issue #31 (item 2) proposes dazpy.materials as a first-class submodule wrapping Iray PBR material setup, alongside the sibling submodules dazpy.cinematics/lighting/poses that already ship. Currently dazpy/ has no materials.py -- only the low-level DazMaterial primitive (_material.py) exists, so downstream users setting up Iray materials (Base Color, texture maps, Metallic/Roughness/Glossy, opacity, etc.) still have to hand-write raw DazScript or chain low-level primitive calls. Scope, per the GH issue's proposed API shape: IrayMaterial (declarative material spec dataclass, mirroring ThreePointLightSetup/HDRIEnvironment's apply_* pattern), TextureMap (texture-slot assignment: diffuse/normal/bump/roughness/metallic/opacity maps with file-existence validation, matching the precedent set by HDRIEnvironment's environment-map path validation), SurfaceProperty (generic named Iray surface-channel get/set, for channels not covered by the typed IrayMaterial fields). Should build on the existing DazMaterial primitive rather than raw script strings, matching the codebase convention (see dazpy/lighting.py, dazpy/poses.py for the apply_*(scene_or_target, spec) pattern to follow).
design: Follow the same design-spec -> plan -> implementation workflow used for dazpy.poses (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-dazpy-poses-design.md) and dazpy.lighting -- start with a design spec doc before writing code.
acceptance_criteria: dazpy/materials.py exists exporting IrayMaterial, TextureMap, SurfaceProperty (or equivalently-scoped names) with an apply_* entrypoint; symbols exported from dazpy/__init__.py top-level package like the other submodules; live-verified against a real DAZ Studio instance per this project's convention (see bu86, GH #32 fixes); unit tests added; CHANGELOG.md entry added.
close_reason: Closed

title: Investigate suppressing/handling modal error dialogs during server-driven renders (GH #34)
description: DAZ Studio pops a blocking 'Error during rendering!' modal on Iray failures, which wedges the main thread and is undismissable in a headless/server-driven workflow. Reporter notes DAZ's headless mode is brittle (some plugins fail to load, preventing Studio from starting). Investigate whether a render-error signal exists that can be hooked before the modal appears, or another way to suppress/auto-dismiss the dialog while a server-driven render is in flight. Optional/exploratory relative to daz-script-server-3l5o and daz-script-server-... which address the plugin-side symptoms; this addresses the root modal itself. (GH issue #34, suggestion #4)
acceptance_criteria: Documented findings on whether the modal can be suppressed or auto-dismissed for server-driven renders, and a decision on whether to implement it.
notes:
RESEARCH FINDINGS (2026-08-15), no code changes:

1. No pre-modal hook exists in the public DAZ Studio 4.5+ SDK. Checked
   dzrendermgr.h (DzRenderMgr: aboutToRender/renderFinished(bool) only),
   dzrenderer.h (DzRenderer: aboutToRender/renderFinished(DzRenderer*),
   killRender(); DiErrorHandler is a RenderMan-style C callback for shader
   compilation errors, not the Iray render-failure path), and
   dzrenderhandler.h (DzRenderHandler: killRender() signal only). None of
   these fire *before* the "Error during rendering!" modal -- they're the
   same signals daz-script-server-3l5o already wired up, which only let us
   react to the busy-state symptom after the fact, not prevent the modal.

2. The modal itself is raised by dzirayrenderer.dll (confirmed present at
   .../DAZStudio4/plugins/dzirayrenderer.dll), a closed-source renderer
   plugin outside the public SDK surface entirely. There's no vtable,
   signal, or setting this project can hook to intercept it before display.

3. No global "silent"/"suppress dialogs" flag exists on DzApp (checked
   dzapp.h in full) that a loaded plugin could toggle at runtime.
   DzApp::GraphicsMode::NoInterface is a construction-time argument to the
   whole application (decided by DAZ Studio's own main(), before any plugin
   loads) -- not reachable from inside a plugin, and per the reporter's own
   note in the original GH #34 report, headless mode is independently
   brittle (some plugins fail to load in it), so it's not a viable target
   even if it were reachable.

4. The remaining option is a generic Qt-level watchdog: a QTimer scanning
   QApplication::topLevelWidgets() for an active modal QDialog/QMessageBox
   and synthesizing a click on its default button, scoped to fire only
   while a server-initiated render is in flight (a state we already track).
   Technically feasible, but explicitly NOT recommended:
     - Requires matching on dialog title/text ("Error during rendering!"),
       which is unversioned, unlocalized-fragile, and could silently break
       or misfire across DAZ Studio releases.
     - No way to scope it to *only* the Iray-error dialog without also
       risking auto-dismissing a legitimate interactive dialog a human user
       is looking at in the same DAZ Studio session (this plugin runs
       alongside normal interactive use, not just headless server use) --
       a false-positive click could discard real work (e.g. an unrelated
       save-conflict prompt) with no way for the user to notice.
     - Attempting to reproduce the exact GH #34 repro (Scene.setBackdrop
       (null) -> Iray DB transaction abort) for live testing was already
       tried during daz-script-server-3l5o and hard-crashed DAZ Studio with
       two different ACCESS_VIOLATION signatures on DS4 and DS6 (see that
       issue's notes, and memory feedback_dazscript_blocking_dialogs) --
       this exact failure mode is inherently unsafe to even test against
       reliably, let alone build automated dialog-clicking logic around.

DECISION: Do not implement auto-dismiss/suppression. The three already-
closed GH #34 fixes (3l5o busy-state clearing, eaub stale-running
watchdog, q0l4 cancel status) already bound the *API-visible* symptom --
/execute fails fast with 503 while a modal blocks the main thread, and
async requests resolve to a terminal status within
ASYNC_STALE_RUNNING_TIMEOUT_MIN (30 min) instead of polling "running"
forever. A blind dialog-clicking watchdog would trade a well-understood,
bounded degradation for an unbounded new failure mode (misclicking a
real dialog) to fix a cosmetic remainder (the human still has to
eventually dismiss the modal or restart DAZ Studio to fully unstick the
main thread). Recommend closing as won't-implement; if unattended/
headless render pipelines become a real requirement later, the safer
answer is an external process-level watchdog that restarts DAZ Studio
when the plugin's /health stops responding, not in-process dialog
suppression.
close_reason: Researched, decided not to implement. See issue notes: no public SDK hook exists to intercept the Iray render-error modal before it appears (raised by closed-source dzirayrenderer.dll, outside SDK surface); no global silent/suppress-dialogs flag on DzApp reachable from a loaded plugin; the only remaining option (a generic Qt dialog-auto-click watchdog) was rejected as too risky -- it could misfire on a legitimate interactive dialog a human is looking at, trading a bounded, well-understood degradation (already fixed by 3l5o/eaub/q0l4: 503 fail-fast + terminal status within 30 min) for an unbounded new failure mode. Recommended external process-level watchdog (restart DAZ Studio on /health timeout) if unattended headless pipelines become a real requirement.

title: dazpy.cinematics: CinematicAnimatedShot (real interpolated keyframes)
description: dazpy.cinematics currently only supports static/per-frame camera placement (CinematicStaticShot, OrbitCamera, FrameSubject — shipped, see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-11-dazpy-cinematics-design.md). GitHub issue #31 also proposed a general CinematicShot concept; the static slice deliberately deferred true interpolated animation. This issue covers CinematicAnimatedShot: a camera move with real DazScript keyframes (addKey or equivalent) rather than per-frame setValue writes. Blocked on confirming DAZ Studio's keyframe/addKey DazScript API against a live instance (unconfirmed as of 2026-08-11) -- same category of research gap as HDRIEnvironment was before it shipped.
close_reason: Shipped CameraKeyframe/CinematicAnimatedShot/apply_animated_shot in dazpy/cinematics.py, plus DazNode.set_position_at_frame/set_rotation_at_frame/clear_position_keys/clear_rotation_keys primitives. Live-verified against a running DAZ Studio 4.x instance (DzNumericProperty.setDoubleValue(tm,val) and DzNode.setWSPos(tm,vec) create real interpolated keyframes; ticks-per-frame is Scene.getTimeStep(), not a fixed constant; new nodes carry a default key that must be cleared first). Discovered and filed daz-script-server-5lpx (existing DazProperty.set_key/is_animated call nonexistent DazScript methods). See design spec addendum in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-11-dazpy-cinematics-design.md.

title: Verify getRenderElementObjects()[3] Environment holder assumption via readback
description:
apply_hdri_environment() and DazRenderSettings' environment setters (_render.py) assume App.getRenderMgr().getRenderElementObjects()[3] is always the Iray Environment Options holder. This was confirmed against exactly one live DAZ Studio 4.x instance during design research for daz-script-server-x6sy. If that index is wrong for a different DAZ Studio version, or reordered, or on the SDK6/Qt6 build this repo also supports, every environment write silently no-ops (matches the existing if (!holder) return; / if (p) ... pattern already used by _set_iray_property) and apply_hdri_environment() returns None as if it succeeded -- the caller has no way to know the HDRI was never applied.

Flagged by the final whole-branch review of the HDRIEnvironment branch (Important #2, non-blocking) as a real gap worth a follow-up rather than a merge blocker, since it's an inherited pattern from pre-existing code (_set_iray_property has the same silent-no-op shape) rather than a new regression.

Suggested fix: add a post-apply readback in apply_hdri_environment (e.g. re-read 'Environment Intensity' via the already-present but currently test-only DazRenderSettings._get_environment_property and compare against what was just set), raising a clear error on mismatch -- mirroring the existing precedent in DazRenderSettings.set_render_engine, whose docstring notes it 'returns only after exact readback' and raises RenderError on disagreement.
close_reason: Added post-apply readback verification (Environment Intensity) in apply_hdri_environment; raises RenderError on holder-unavailable or mismatch instead of silently no-oping

title: Research and implement dazpy.lighting HDRIEnvironment (IBL/dome lighting)
description: GitHub issue #31 proposed dazpy.lighting.HDRIEnvironment alongside ThreePointLightSetup and SetLightColor. ThreePointLightSetup shipped (daz-script-server-p1af); SetLightColor needed no new code (already covered by DazLight.set_color). HDRIEnvironment was explicitly deferred during design (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-07-dazpy-lighting-design.md) because no dome/environment-map DazScript primitive currently exists in dazpy -- this needs research into what DAZ Studio actually exposes for Iray environment/IBL lighting (DzUberEnvironmentShader or similar) before a design can be written.
close_reason: Shipped: design spec + plan (docs/superpowers/specs|plans/2026-08-07-dazpy-hdri-environment*.md), HDRIEnvironment dataclass, apply_hdri_environment, validated environment-map setter, package exports, and readback verification (daz-script-server-jnbm) — all landed across commits 691d04c..b62ca4c

title: Add coordinate-system & vector math conversion utilities
description: GitHub issue #31 (item 4): Daz Studio uses Y-up with idiosyncrasies (e.g. Genesis 9 facing +Z, Y-rotation inversion on cameras) that force every downstream integration (Blender, Unreal) to reimplement coordinate conversion. Proposed dazpy.math helper module with functions like daz_yup_to_blender_zup() and fix_camera_orientation(). dazpy/math3.py currently provides Vec3/Quat/BoundingBox math primitives but no coordinate-space conversion helpers -- this would build on top of those.
close_reason: Added AxisRemap to dazpy/math3.py: apply_vec3/apply_quat/apply_bbox with reflection rejection, Y_UP_TO_Z_UP preset, exported from dazpy package. Wired into tests.py unit runner.

title: Add domain submodules (cinematics, lighting, materials, poses)
description: GitHub issue #31 (item 2) proposes packaging common DazScript macros into first-class Python submodules to avoid downstream users writing raw DazScript for common scene-choreography tasks: dazpy.cinematics (OrbitCamera, CinematicShot, FrameSubject), dazpy.lighting (ThreePointLightSetup, HDRIEnvironment, SetLightColor), dazpy.materials (IrayMaterial, TextureMap, SurfaceProperty), dazpy.poses (ApplyPose, ResetTransforms, ZeroFigure). None of these modules currently exist in dazpy/. Should build on existing DazNode/DazCamera/DazLight/DazMaterial primitives rather than raw script strings.
notes: dazpy.poses shipped (apply_pose, reset_transforms, zero_figure) -- see docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-10-dazpy-poses-design.md and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-10-dazpy-poses.md. zero_figure defaults to include_props=False after final review found the True/apply_full path could zero the figure's root Scale/transform via DzNode's generic property enumeration -- True remains available as an explicit opt-in. Remaining GH #31 domain submodules: dazpy.cinematics, dazpy.materials.
close_reason: All four proposed GH #31 domain submodules shipped: dazpy.poses (apply_pose/reset_transforms/zero_figure), dazpy.materials (IrayMaterial/TextureMap/SurfaceProperty, daz-script-server-no7b), dazpy.cinematics (CinematicStaticShot/OrbitCamera/FrameSubject/CinematicAnimatedShot, daz-script-server-v6sk), dazpy.lighting (ThreePointLightSetup/HDRIEnvironment/set_light_color, daz-script-server-q16y). All build on existing DazNode/DazCamera/DazLight/DazMaterial primitives per the original design constraint.

title: Pool DazClient connections via requests.Session + add close()/context-manager
description: DazClient currently issues each HTTP call via bare requests.post()/get() (module-level function calls), creating a fresh TCP connection per request instead of reusing a pooled connection. AsyncDazClient (added in 2.9.0, dazpy.aio) uses a persistent httpx.AsyncClient with close()/async-context-manager support. Bring DazClient to parity: back it with a requests.Session for connection pooling/keep-alive, and add close()/__enter__/__exit__ so sync callers can also do 'with DazClient() as client:'.
close_reason: DazClient now uses a pooled requests.Session for all HTTP calls (post/get/delete, including streaming), and gained close()/__enter__/__exit__ for parity with AsyncDazClient. Updated TestErrorMapping in tests/test_dazpy.py to mock the session instead of module-level requests.post; added close()/context-manager tests. Full test_dazpy.py suite (540 tests) + test_dazpy_aio.py (21 tests) pass.

title: Replace raw dict returns with typed models (dataclasses/Pydantic)
description: dazpy methods currently return raw dicts for structured values (e.g. {x,y,z,w} quaternions, bounding boxes, scene snapshots) rather than typed objects, so callers get no IDE autocompletion or runtime validation. math3.py already has Vec3/Quat/BoundingBox for math ops -- evaluate extending those (or adding lightweight dataclasses/Pydantic models) as the return type for node/camera/light/material property accessors across dazpy/_node.py, _camera.py, _light.py, _material.py, etc.
close_reason: Won't implement: decided against typed Pydantic/dataclass return models for node/camera/light/material property accessors -- raw dict returns are being kept as the API surface. GH #31 closed with this as the one item not pursued.

title: FaceID face-identity pass doesn't preserve hair color
description: IPAdapter FaceID's embedding (docs/examples/rendering/sprite_matrix/) encodes facial features only, not hair color. Since the SAM-refined face-detailer crop covers hair as well as face (needed to avoid a hairline color seam, see bbox_dilation), and the pass no longer starts from real source pixels (SetDefaultImageForSEGS was removed), hair color is unconstrained during refinement and can drift from the source. Confirmed live on a grey-haired test character (jason_a): hair rendered brown/blonde across the entire tested denoise (0.15-0.35) x faceid_weight (0.8-1.2) grid, independent of both knobs. User explicitly chose to ship with this documented as a known limitation (README.md, config.py) rather than pause to fix it. Filed as follow-up in case it becomes worth revisiting -- e.g. a secondary hair-color-only conditioning signal, or constraining just a hair sub-region to real pixels while still FaceID-conditioning the face.
close_reason: Confirmed resolved via live testing against jason_a and abby_b, following the daz-script-server-3os rebuild (single-pass + lineart composite, replacing FaceDetailer/IPAdapterFaceID) and the r5br negative-prompt/Canny-threshold follow-up fix for a newly-surfaced artifact (harsh facial ink lines from the style LoRA, distinct from toe's original pale-skin/split-shadow symptoms but found during the same live-tuning pass). No pale/ghostlike skin, no harsh eye-shadow, no facial pencil-mark lines, no hair-color seam artifact (no more crop boundary to desync at) on either character.

title: Add render_shot.py: single-shot variant of sprite matrix pipeline
description: Simplified variant of the sprite matrix pipeline that assumes pose/expression are already set up by hand in the live Daz scene and starts directly at the render step. No JSON spec, no pose/expression preset library -- plain CLI flags, single named shot, front/back render + optional ComfyUI stylize, reusing paths.py/canvas_convert.py/workflow_builder.py/comfyui_client.py from the batch pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: render_shot.py compiles, --dry-run works, unit tests for pure helpers pass
close_reason: Implemented render_shot.py + tests, verified dry-run and unit tests pass.

title: Bounded-wait backstop for the residual busy-detection race window
description:
Both signal-based (SceneEventBroker depth counter) and DzProgress/DzBackgroundProgress busy detection are now live on feature/studio-busy-handling (commit 720736f), and together catch the large majority of a scene load's busy window. Live testing (3 File->Open runs) found a residual gap: the trailing node-streaming phase after sceneLoaded() fires appears to run as several chained sub-operations, each apparently its own progress instance, with brief gaps between them where neither DzScene signals nor DzProgress::isActive()/DzBackgroundProgress::isActive() report busy. A request whose busy check runs during one of those gaps still commits to the blocking Qt::BlockingQueuedConnection call and waits out the remainder of that phase -- observed up to ~15s in testing, bounded by scene complexity, not indefinite like the pre-fix behavior, but still a real (if much smaller and rarer) block-then-succeed window instead of a clean fast 503.

Decision (2026-07-23, live testing session): ship the current two-signal detection as-is rather than close this fully now -- it's already a large improvement over the original unbounded hang. This issue tracks the deferred, more invasive fix: cap how long any HTTP thread can actually block on the main-thread invokeMethod call itself (independent of whether busy detection correctly predicted the state in advance), so even an undetected busy window can't hang past a bound. This was originally proposed as 'Approach 3' in the initial design brainstorming for this feature (bounded wait + fallback to async-style response) and revisited as a live option during testing.

Design note: the underlying BlockingQueuedConnection call can't be cancelled once queued -- a timeout on the calling side would leave an orphaned queued call that still executes on the main thread later, with its result discarded. Needs a decision on what the HTTP response contract looks like in that case (plain 503 retry, or auto-convert to the async-request-tracking flow so the result isn't lost). See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-22-studio-busy-handling-design.md for the original design and docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-22-studio-busy-handling.md for the implementation plan this extends.
close_reason: Won't fix, after implementation review. The already-shipped pre-check busy detection (commit 720736f, on master) already turns the original unbounded hang into a bounded, self-correcting ~15s slow-but-correct response — no data loss, no wrong result, just latency. A working bounded-wait backstop was implemented and independently verified concurrency-correct (race-free CAS ceiling, sound thread/promise lifetimes, Qt6-portable), but final review surfaced a real behavioral hazard: on timeout the queued main-thread call is NOT cancelled (Qt has no API for this) and keeps running, so the 503 the client receives is misleading (the operation is still executing), and dazpy's retry_on_busy could re-run it — a double-execution risk strictly worse than the slow-but-correct wait it replaces. The default 20s timeout also exceeds the one measured gap (~15s), so it offers little value against the observed problem and is really speculative insurance against a worse, never-observed wedged-main-thread case. Decision: the tradeoff isn't worth it as scoped; keep the existing pre-check detection only. The implementation (branch feature/studio-busy-handling, commits 680b267..467ea7b) is not merged to master. Revisit only if a genuinely unbounded hang is observed in practice, with a design that avoids the discard-and-maybe-retry hazard (e.g. never reusing a retry-safe error code for a timeout that doesn't actually stop the underlying work).

title: Harden main-thread busy state with a depth counter if DAZ nests scene signals
description: SceneEventBroker's busy-state tracker (src/SceneEventBroker.cpp) uses a single scalar reset to Idle unconditionally in each *Finished/*Cleared/*Loaded/*Saved slot. If DAZ Studio ever nests scene-clear signals inside a scene-load (loadStarting -> clearStarting -> cleared -> ... -> loaded), onSceneCleared would reset busy to Idle while the load is still blocking the main thread, briefly reopening the indefinite-hang window. Flagged by final whole-branch review of feature/studio-busy-handling (commit 89aaafd). Gate this on what daz-script-server-fbk's manual smoke test observes -- only needed if nesting is actually confirmed. Fix: replace the scalar with a depth counter (increment on *Starting, decrement on *Finished, busy = count>0).
notes: Fix implemented on feature/studio-busy-handling commit 474244d (depth counter via enterBusy/exitBusy). Confirmed real via live testing under daz-script-server-fbk, not just hypothetical. Will close once fbk's re-test confirms the fix resolves the observed hang.
close_reason: Fixed on feature/studio-busy-handling commit 474244d (depth counter). Confirmed real via live File->Open testing -- old scalar design reset busy mid-load when a nested scene.clear_starting/cleared fired inside scene.loading.

title: DPB: reinstall/versioning semantics for plugin drops
description: Define what happens when a dropped zip manifest id matches an already-installed plugin -- should behave like the existing script registry convention, name is ID and overwrites existing, not silently fail or require a version-bump prompt.
design: On id match: stop the plugin running warm worker first, necessary on Windows since a live python.exe holds file locks on its own venv, extract and validate via the staged-install flow, atomically swap into the plugin dir, re-run eager dependency resolution so status cycles resolving to ready again, and log the version transition explicitly, matching the existing DSS log line format. Worker respawn stays lazy -- next invocation after reinstall spawns fresh with the new code.
acceptance_criteria: Dropping a zip with an existing plugin id replaces it cleanly with no stale worker holding old code or file locks, and the version change is visible in the log.
close_reason: Dead duplicate from an incomplete migration -- real completed copies are daz-python-bridge-sop.6/.8 (closed).

title: Iray Canvas: programmatically add new canvas types (normal/depth/material-ID)
description: Tier 2 of daz-script-server-llr. Scope: create new Iray canvas entries by type (e.g. normal, depth/Z, material-ID, object-ID) entirely via script, without requiring the canvas to already exist in the scene from prior manual setup in the Render Settings > Advanced > Canvases UI. This is the larger, less-certain lift referenced in GitHub issue #19 gaps #1 -- needs SDK/live-instance research into whether DzIrayRenderer exposes an addCanvas()-style API or equivalent, since this is not confirmed the way the existing quality-preset properties are. Depends on tier 1 (reading/enabling existing canvases and retrieving output paths) landing first so the output-path plumbing can be reused.

title: Add camera lens shift access to dazpy
description: GitHub issue #19 gap #6: dazpy/_camera.py exposes near_clipping_plane/far_clipping_plane (read-only) but has no lens_shift property. Accurate depth-based effects (fog, DOF-driven line weight) depend on exact lens shift values matching what the render engine uses. Add a lens_shift read (and setter if the underlying DzCamera node exposes one) accessor alongside the existing clip-plane properties.
close_reason: Added lens_shift_x/lens_shift_y read/write properties to DazCamera, backed by the 'Lens Shift X/Y (mm)' properties confirmed against a live instance

title: Return resolved output path from DazRenderSettings.render()/render_and_wait()
description: GitHub issue #19 gap #4: the high-level dazpy._render_api.render()/render_variants() API already returns RenderResult.output_path, but the lower-level DazRenderSettings.render()/render_and_wait() in dazpy/_render.py still returns only a bool. Change these to also return the resolved output file path (mirroring what doRender()/opts.renderImgFilename actually wrote) so client code doesn't have to guess or duplicate the path-resolution logic.
close_reason: DazRenderSettings.render()/render_and_wait() now return a RenderOutcome(success, output_path) dataclass instead of a bare bool -- output_path is read back from opts.renderImgFilename after doRender() so it reflects what was actually written. Verified with 3 new unit tests (mocked) and 1 live integration test (real 64x64/4-sample render, confirmed file written to resolved path).

title: Add active_engine() query to DazRenderSettings
description: GitHub issue #19 gap: dazpy can already SET the active render engine (engine param on POST /render and /render/batch, mapped to DzIrayRenderer/Dz3DelightRenderer/DzFilamentRenderer via renderMgr.setActiveRenderer in DzScriptServerPane.cpp), but there is no getter to query which engine is currently active. Add an active_engine() (or engine property) read accessor on DazRenderSettings in dazpy/_render.py, backed by App.getRenderMgr().getActiveRenderer().
close_reason: Added active_engine() to dazpy/_render.py, backed by getActiveRenderer().className() mapped to friendly names

title: DS4 (Qt 4.8) cannot build for arm64: qatomic_powerpc.h asm constraint error
description: DAZStudio4.5+ SDK bundles Qt 4.8, which predates Apple Silicon and has no real arm64 atomics support. CI run 29248727943 confirmed: building DazScriptServer for arm64 against DS4/Qt4 fails at DAZStudio4.5+ SDK/include/QtCore/qatomic_powerpc.h:126 and :143 with 'error: invalid output constraint =&b in asm' — Qt4's platform detection falls back to a bogus PowerPC atomics path on arm64 rather than a real arm64 implementation. This was previously masked by the CMakeLists.txt CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES FORCE bug (fixed in master 43ca8ce), which silently built x86_64 even when arm64/universal was requested. Unlike the DS6 case (daz-script-server-250, missing arm64 SDK lib), this is a Qt4 SDK/toolchain limitation with no likely fix from DAZ; probably means DS4 macOS builds should stay x86_64-only for the foreseeable future. build-macos.yml's macos-arm-ds4 and macos-universal-ds4 legs are currently red until this is addressed (see also test-build.yml's build-macos-arm-ds4 job).
acceptance_criteria: Either DS4 arm64 compiles successfully, or build-macos.yml explicitly skips sdk-version=4 + arm64/universal with a clear message (matching the DS6 guard) instead of failing red
close_reason: Decision: DAZ Studio 6 itself is an x86_64 build running under Rosetta 2 on Apple Silicon, so an x86_64-only plugin (DS4 or DS6) works fine there and native arm64 isn't actually required. We still build/publish 'Apple Silicon' named plugin artifacts for naming-consistency, but the build workflows stay as-is (force-compiling x86_64 for these legs). No further arm64 SDK/toolchain work needed.

description: daz-studio-6-sdk-macos (bluemoonfoundry/daz-studio-sdks) ships a single Mac64/ dir containing an x86_64-only libdzcore.dylib. CI run 29248380358 confirmed: linking DazScriptServer for arm64 against this SDK fails with 'ld: warning: ignoring file libdzcore.dylib: found architecture x86_64, required architecture arm64' then 'ld: symbol(s) not found for architecture arm64'. This is a DAZ Studio 6 SDK limitation, not a repo config bug — the CMakeLists.txt CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES FORCE bug (fixed in daz-script-server master commit 43ca8ce) was masking this by silently building x86_64 even when arm64 was requested. build-macos.yml now explicitly skips the sdk-version=6 + arm64/universal combo with a clear CI summary message instead of failing red. This issue tracks getting an arm64 (or universal) libdzcore.dylib published to daz-studio-sdks so the DS6 Apple Silicon leg can actually build.

Verified on a real M4 Mac that DAZ Studio 6 itself still runs under Rosetta 2 there (Activity Monitor shows Kind=Intel), so an x86_64-only DS6 plugin loads and runs fine, and CI's macos-arm-ds6 leg now builds/uploads successfully (run 29294737055) instead of being skipped. This issue remains open: the real fix (DAZ publishing a native arm64 libdzcore.dylib) hasn't happened; the acceptance criteria is unchanged.

title: Fix sleeve/arm length: use 3D diagonal distance instead of Y-only
description: Sleeve length reports 35.7 cm on G9 base figure (expected ~58-62 cm). The _vertical_distance() helper measures only the Y-coordinate difference. In A-pose the arm slopes ~31 degrees downward, so vertical drop from shoulder (y=135) to hand (y=100) is 35 cm but the actual arm length is ~60 cm. Fix: compute Euclidean distance (sqrt dx^2+dy^2+dz^2) for limb length measurements where the limb is likely angled. At minimum document this limitation prominently in the output. Affects sleeve_length, and potentially front_waist_length and inseam when figure is not in T-pose. Verified live on Genesis 9 base figure 2026-06-18.
close_reason: Replaced _vertical_distance(shoulder_y, wrist_y) with _3d_distance(shoulder_xyz, wrist_xyz) using new _find_anchor_xyz/_avg_pair_xyz helpers. Captures true 3D arm diagonal in A-pose instead of Y-axis-only drop. Note added to output indicating shoulder anchor is inner clavicle not acromion.

title: Fix shoulder width: l_shoulder is inner clavicle joint not outer acromion tip
description: Shoulder width reports 6.91 cm on G9 (expected 38-42 cm). The l_shoulder bone origin sits at the inner shoulder joint (x=3.45 cm from center), which is the clavicle-to-arm attachment point, not the acromion/shoulder-tip. Fix: use the wider span across the mesh at shoulder height (e.g. X-span of the torso contour at spine4 level, or use l_upperarm at x=16 as a better approximation). Verified live on Genesis 9 base figure 2026-06-18.
close_reason: Replaced _bone_pair_x_span(shoulder_left_bones) with shoulder_width_left/right_bones fields in FigureProfile. G9 now uses l_upperarm/r_upperarm (humeral head, x≈16cm from center) instead of l_shoulder/r_shoulder (inner clavicle joint, x=3.45cm). G8/8.1 keeps lShldrBend which was already reasonable.

title: Unit and integration tests for comfyui_enhance example
description:
Write tests for all components of the comfyui_enhance example project.

## Why
The ComfyUI client and file watcher have non-trivial logic (polling, retry, write-completion detection) that must be unit tested with mocks. An integration test validates the full pipeline against real servers.

## What needs to be done
- tests/test_comfyui_client.py:
  - test upload_image: mock POST /upload/image, assert returns correct ref
  - test queue_prompt: mock POST /prompt, assert prompt_id extracted
  - test wait_for_result: mock polling with 'pending' then 'complete' responses
  - test wait_for_result timeout: assert TimeoutError raised after deadline
  - test download_image: mock GET /view, assert bytes returned
  - test ComfyUIError on non-2xx response

- tests/test_file_watcher.py:
  - test watch() detects file created in temp dir
  - test watch() timeout raises TimeoutError
  - test write-completion: file that grows then stabilizes triggers only after stable

- tests/test_workflow_builder.py:
  - test build() returns dict with required ComfyUI node keys
  - test parameter substitution (checkpoint_name, denoise, steps)

- tests/test_integration.py (skipped when servers unavailable):
  - @skip_no_daz: capture viewport, assert file exists
  - @skip_no_comfyui: upload+queue+wait+download full round trip

## Acceptance criteria
- All unit tests pass without any live servers
- Integration tests skip gracefully when servers are unavailable
- pytest tests/test_*.py all green

title: Document render API with VN workflow examples
description:
The render API design includes a non-obvious batch interleaving pattern that needs explicit documentation and examples to be useful for VN pipeline authors.

Add to README / dazpy docs:
1. Basic single render example
2. Batch variant rendering — pattern A (submit all upfront, poll)
3. Batch variant rendering — pattern B (interleave scene setup between renders for complex changes)
4. Multi-figure scene example (two characters, different expressions)
5. Note on transparent backgrounds: iRay scene setup controls this; the API does not manipulate backdrop nodes

Emphasize in pattern B docs: because renders are sequential in the async queue, a client can submit render N, wait for it to start, execute scene-setup scripts to configure render N+1, then submit render N+1 — achieving tight coupling between renders without the server needing to understand the full variant state.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add dazpy render API (render, render_variants)
description:
dazpy needs high-level Python wrappers for the render endpoints so VN pipeline scripts can trigger renders without constructing raw HTTP requests or parsing SSE streams manually.

Implement in dazpy:
  DazScriptServer.render(output_path, *, figure, morphs, figures, width, height, camera, engine, wait=True, timeout=300) -> RenderResult
  DazScriptServer.render_variants(variants, base=None, *, on_progress=None) -> list[RenderResult]

Dataclasses:
  FigureMorphs(name: str|None, morphs: dict[str, float])
  RenderVariant(output_path, figure, morphs, figures, width, height)
  RenderBase(figure, width, height, camera, engine)
  RenderResult(success, output_path, file_size_bytes, duration_ms, error)

render() uses SSE progress stream when available, falls back to polling. render_variants() submits via /render/batch and tracks all request_ids, calling on_progress with (completed, total) after each render finishes.
close_reason: Closed

title: dazpy.lighting: standalone set_light_color helper for GH #31 API parity
description: GitHub issue #31 (item 2b) proposed dazpy.lighting.SetLightColor as part of the lighting submodule's public surface. Light color setting already works today via the low-level DazLight.set_color(r,g,b) primitive (dazpy/_light.py), and is used internally by apply_three_point_light_setup via LightSpec.color -- so this is a minor API-parity gap, not a missing capability. Decide whether to add a small apply_*-style standalone helper (e.g. dazpy.lighting.set_light_color(scene, node_name, color)) for consistency with the rest of the submodule's public API, or close this as won't-fix since DazLight.set_color already covers the use case.
close_reason: Added dazpy.lighting.set_light_color(light, r, g, b) as a thin submodule-level entry point for DazLight.set_color, for GH #31 API parity. While live-verifying against a running DAZ Studio 4.x instance, found and fixed a real pre-existing bug: DazLight.set_color() looked up a property labeled 'Diffuse Color' via findPropertyByLabel and called .setValue() on it -- that property doesn't exist on any light type (point/distant/spot all confirmed live); the real property is 'Color', a DzColorProperty requiring .setColorValue(new Color(...)) not .setValue(...). The old code silently no-op'd (guarded by 'if (p)') so light colors set via DazLight.set_color or apply_three_point_light_setup's LightSpec.color were never actually applied. Fixed dazpy/_light.py and its mock test; live-verified the fix round-trips correctly via getDiffuseColor().

title: AxisRemap polish: docs, __eq__, dead state, _mat3_to_quat branch coverage
description:
Follow-up from the final review of daz-script-server-okpk (AxisRemap coordinate conversion, merged in af4bb11). Four Minor items were deferred rather than blocking merge:

1. docs/api/math3.rst and README.md's math3 blurb were never updated to mention AxisRemap/Y_UP_TO_Z_UP.
2. AxisRemap has no __eq__/__hash__ (Vec3 and Quat both do). If added, must add both together (eq without hash makes instances unhashable).
3. AxisRemap._matrix and _det are stored on the instance but never read after construction except via the _rotation_quat gate; harmless dead state, low priority.
4. dazpy/math3.py's _mat3_to_quat has 4 branches (trace>0 plus 3 diagonal-dominant cases); the shipped test suite in tests/test_math3.py only exercises the trace>0 branch. Two independent reviewers verified the other 3 branches correct out-of-band during review, but there's no regression test protecting them. A property-based test sweeping all 24 proper axis permutations (see the final review's suggested test) would close this permanently.

Also worth considering as a separate, larger follow-up (not part of this issue): an AxisRemap.inverse() method, since round-tripping currently requires hand-deriving the inverse remap by hand.
acceptance_criteria: All four items addressed or explicitly triaged as won't-fix with reasoning.
close_reason: Docs updated (README + math3.rst), AxisRemap gained __eq__/__hash__, removed dead _matrix/_det slots (kept as locals), added 24-permutation property test covering all _mat3_to_quat branches. inverse() deliberately left as separate future item per issue note.
